The damage path of an EF-1 tornado was identified over inaccessible rural marsh areas of southern Tangipahoa Parish. This radar confirmed tornado had a peak rotational velocity of near 40 knots and a tornado debris signature visible up to approximately 5300 feet. The tornado tracked over mostly marsh within the Joyce Wildlife Management Area. Highest resolution satellite data available from January 2017 showed evidence of broken branches and numerous uprooted trees along the Sinking Bayou. The tornado tracked northeast and grew in size and strength of the marsh peaking at around 200 yards in width which coincided well with the KLIX radar data. Additional displaced trees were identified along a separate canal around this time. The tornado then quickly weakened and occluded by 17:00 UTC as corroborated by the waning radar signature.

The damage path of a short-lived EF-1 tornado was identified on high resolution satellite imagery in rural southern Amite County, MS. This tornado began northwest of the intersection of Powell Rd and Street Rd where it displaced a few trees. The tornado then crossed Street Rd and moved over inaccessible forested areas near the West Fork Amite River where it produced a defined swath of tree damage evident on high resolution satellite imagery that was approximately 90 yards wide. The damage path then became more sparse and less defined after it crossed the river and only minor tree damage was identified which is where the tornado was estimated to have lifted.

The damage path of a strong EF-1 tornado was identified on high resolution satellite imagery over rural southern Amite County, MS. A defined path of tree damage began just east of S Greensburg Rd and moved eastward where tree damage gradually became more significant as it crossed a few small rural roads. The tornado peaked in intensity with sustained winds of approximately 110 mph near the East Fork Amite River where larger swaths (150 yards wide) were identified via high resolution satellite imagery. The tornado gradually weakened as it crossed River Rd causing smaller swaths of uprooted/damaged trees, and it's estimated the tornado lifted south of Bennet Rd as there was no further conclusive damage evident beyond this point.

The damage path of an EF-0 tornado was identified via high resolution satellite imagery over rural parts of western Pearl River County, east of Henleyfield, MS. This tornado was embedded within a line of storms and produced evident displacement of trees and defoliation between Carey Byrd Rd and Harry Sones Rd. This was well collocated with a tight, coherent tornado vortex signature on KLIX radar data.

High resolution satellite imagery in conjunction with a thunderstorm wind damage report helped to identify a 7.5 mile-long damage path of an EF-1 tornado east of Osyka in Pike County, MS. This damage path began near Foxchase Rd in close relation to the tornado vortex signature on KLIX radar imagery from the January 21st, 2017 squall line. Minor tree damage became increasingly more notable on high resolution satellite imagery as the tornado crossed Mount Zion Rd. The tornado maintained EF-1 intensity as it tracked east-northeast causing damage to three mobile homes, one of which was moved off its blocks at Ed Brumfield Rd. The tornado continued east producing patches to swaths of tree damage along a focused path in rural Pike County, south of Osyka Progress Rd. These swaths of tree damage were the basis for the peak intensity rating of 100 mph EF-1. Additional notable swaths of tree damage to pine trees were noted north of Blazo Rd. The tornado began to gradually weaken as it crossed Shady Grove Rd, but even still roof and wall panels of a hay barn were evidently removed and additional tree damage was identifiable. More tree damage was noted east of this point where the path apparently concludes near Smithburg Rd. The exact start and end points are estimated and time matched with radar imagery.

A combination of local storm reports and high resolution satellite imagery helped to identify the track of an EF-0 tornado that occurred between Norco and Kenner, LA. This tornado developed near Airline Highway, just east of several refineries. A report of trees and power lines being downed on East Harding St further backed this satellite analysis. Sporadic patches of tree damage were evident on satellite imagery which continued eastward crossing Airline Hwy and into open marsh areas of St. Charles Parish. The most notable swath of tree damage occurred north of the I-310 and Airline Hwy interchange. The tornado then crossed I-310 causing minor vegetation damage near Decatur St. The tornado crossed briefly into Jefferson Parish where it uprooted a single tree and displaced an outdoor shed before lifting.

A combination of local storm reports and high resolution satellite imagery helped to identify the track of an EF-0 tornado that occurred between Norco and Kenner, LA. This tornado developed near Airline Highway, just east of several refineries. A report of trees and power lines being downed on East Harding St further backed this satellite analysis. Sporadic patches of tree damage were evident on satellite imagery which continued eastward crossing Airline Hwy and into open marsh areas of St. Charles Parish. The most notable swath of tree damage occurred north of the I-310 and Airline Hwy interchange. The tornado then crossed I-310 causing minor vegetation damage near Decatur St. The tornado crossed briefly into Jefferson Parish where it uprooted a single tree and displaced an outdoor shed before lifting.

A weak tornadic waterspout moved onshore north of Ruddock, LA in St. John Parish. This tornado caused only minor damage to marsh vegetation and caused a small, defined path evident on high resolution satellite imagery. It's unclear if the tornadic waterspout continued northwest into Lake Maurepas as radar presentation continued to weaken and broaden as it moved offshore.

The damage path of an EF-0 tornado was identified on high resolution satellite imagery over rural and inaccessible parts of southeast Amite County near McDaniel Ln and Brabham Rd. The tornado produced minor tree damage along a coherent path that included a lumber farm where trees were cleared quickly after the toward making it difficult to discern the severity of damage in this location. The tornado lifted quickly after crossing the county line into Pike County, near Old Mill Rd.

The intermittent damage path of an EF-0 tornado was identified via high resolution satellite imagery over rural Pike County which tracked east across Interstate 55 before lifting near Magnolia, MS. The tornado only caused minor tree damage including a few uproots visible on satellite imagery. No structures were reported to have received damage from this tornado. This damage path was well-aligned with an embedded, tight tornado vortex signature on KLIX radar data.

The track of an EF-0 tornado was identified over inaccessible parts of St. Charles Parish east of Lac Des Allemands using high resolution satellite imagery. This tornado tracked from northwest to southeast causing patchy tree damage throughout its track. The most notable vegetation damage was about a 100-yard-wide swath of tree damage near Providence Canal concurrent with a high-end EF-0.

The track of an EF-0 tornado was identified over inaccessible parts of St. Charles Parish east of Lac Des Allemands using high resolution satellite imagery. This tornado tracked from northwest to southeast causing patchy tree damage throughout its track. The most notable vegetation damage was about a 100-yard-wide swath of tree damage near Providence Canal concurrent with a high-end EF-0.

An EF-1 tornado with estimated maximum winds of 110 mph quickly developed and tracked across the Pearl River basin between Hickory, LA and Nicholson, MS. This tornado started near the Pearl River where it quickly grew in size and strength. The tornado peaked in strength causing a 200-yard-wide swath of deforestation visible on high resolution satellite imagery which was largely due to uproots and snaps. This damage path narrowed and weakened as it raced off to the northeast. Additional patches of high-end EF-0 and low-end EF-1 tree damage were identified over the Pearl River Basin as the tornado crossed into Mississippi. Additional EF-0 tree damage was identified on high resolution satellite imagery near Jackson Landing Road which was collocated with the tornado debris signature apparent on KLIX radar. The tornado appears to have lifted shortly after this point as the radar signature weakens and no further damage was identified.

A weak EF-0 tornado damage path was identified on high resolution satellite imagery near the Wolf River and Cemetery Rd in Harrison County, MS. Only minor defoliation and damage to tree tops was noted on satellite imagery with a more noticeable minor patch of tree damage near the bank of the Wolf River. This damage path is collocated with a tornado debris signature that was evident on KLIX radar imagery from May 11, 2019.

An EF-0 tornado damage path was identified in rural Harrison County, MS near McHenry Road. The tornado damage path consisted predominantly of minor softwood tree damage visible on high resolution satellite imagery. Maximum sustained winds were estimated near 80 mph based on high snaps of tree tops south of McHenry Rd.

Minor vegetation damage was identified using high resolution satellite imagery to verify the track of a radar-confirmed EF-0 tornado that occurred near Blind River, southeast of Denson, LA in Livingston Parish. This weak tornado remained away from any structures though a weak, but conclusive tornado debris signature was visible on KHDC radar imagery which aligned with intermittent minor vegetation over the marsh. Most notably a few trees were visibly displaced on the bank of Blind River.

An EF-1 tornado touched down on the northwest side of the Hammond Northshore Regional Airport just before 4am CDT where patches of large branches were snapped. The tornado continued to the north-northwest across highways 443 and 1064 where it maintained EF-0 strength by snapping small branches. The tornado remained over rural parts of northern Hammond while steadily picking up strength. The tornado was nearing peak intensity as it approached the intersection of Faller Rd and Tycer Ln at 4:06am where a house lost an awning and parts of its roof. The tornado finally reach peak intensity at as it continued to the north-northwest and approaches the intersection of Faller Rd and McManus Dr. Here, a hardwood tree was snapped in the middle. The tornado maintained this peak intensity as it approached Highway 442 where a few more hardwood trees were snapped. The tornado began weakening after this point as is continued to make its way to the north-northwest and across the Tangipahoa River. As it crossed the river, it practically paralleled S Bennett Rd in Independence, LA where it mainly snapped large branches until it lifted shortly before Highway 40 at 4:14am.

A brief EF-0 touched down just north of Highway 445 on Bailey Loop Rd in Loranger, LA at 4:57am CDT where it broke off patches of large branches. This tornado continued due northward into forested areas of Loranger before making it to Bradford Ln at 5:04am. Here, more patches of small and large branches were broken before the tornado lifted along Highway 40 still at 5:04am.

An EF-1 touched down south of Robert, LA at 5:11am CDT along Traino Rd where a few small limbs were snapped. The tornado quickly gained strength as it moved north towards Highway 22. The tornado reached peak intensity as a 90mph EF-1 at 5:14am along Highway 20 just east of the Fairhope Subdivision where a group of softwood trees were snapped. This tornado maintained peak intensity as it continued northward towards Crown Dr at 5:18am. Here more softwood trees were snapped and a roof was partially removed from a manufactured home. The tornado began to weaken and occlude as it moved to the northeast. The tornado broke small limbs and caused small trees to lean in a convergent pattern before lifting at 5:21am just southwest of Jasper Ln south of Robert, LA.

An EF-0 tornado crossed Bear Island Road south of Hwy 22, causing damage mostly to trees. One home suffered minor roof damage, and a large metal canopy was thrown about 25 to 40 yard to the southeast. High resolution satellite imagery helped to identify the start and end of this tornado over the inaccessible marsh areas where defoliation and minor tree damage were evident. The marsh damage was also collocated with an evident tornado debris signature on KHDC radar imagery.

The damage path of an EF-1 tornado was identified via high resolution satellite imagery over inaccessible rural marsh areas of Terrebonne Parish, southwest of Humphreys, LA. This tornado began southwest of Blue Bird Canal where a defined, but weak path of damage to marsh vegetation was evident. The marsh damage continued northeast across Blue Bird Canal, narrowly missing fishing camps, and was collocated with a strong tornado vortex signature on KHDC radar imagery. The tornado intensified as it crossed the Intracoastal Waterway and Lake Hackberry with numerous displaced trees evident along a canal and maximum path width around 250 yards. This was collocated with a tornado debris signature that was identified on Climavision V014 radar imagery. The tornado continued northeast and quickly weakened which is corroborated by KHDC and Climavision radar imagery. The tornado evidently lifted prior to reaching structures along Bayou Black Drive in Humphreys.

An EF-1 tornado was confirmed by NWS ground survey northeast of Hammond, LA in Tangipahoa Parish. The ground survey first noted damage near River Rd and Arbuthnott Drive. The tornado moved generally northward to the east of River Rd causing additional damage mostly to trees. The strongest damage surveyed was along Dummyline Rd where it snapped several large trees, before the tornado crossed the Tangipahoa River. It then caused additional tree damage and destroyed a tent on the grounds of Camp Living Waters. Remote survey techniques utilizing high-resolution satellite imagery identified additional damage just north of Dusty Ln between Diana Ln and Calmes Ln, as a start point. The same imagery also indicated the tornado continued past the cap ground, causing tree damage near Robert Perkins Rd, and gradually weakening and lifting as it approached Chappepeela Rd.

A photographer filmed a waterspout over Lake Pontchartrain just east of the Causeway Bridge a few miles south of Mandeville. Drone footage was key to confirming that this in fact a waterspout and not just a funnel.

A defined, narrow damage path was identified in the marsh grass near the mouth of the Jourdan River. This damage path was visible after an associated tornado vortex signature visible on KLIX radar passed over this area on January 11, 2020. No apparent damage indicators could be identified using high resolution satellite imagery.

An EF-1 tornado touched down south of Brewster Road in Saint Tammany Parish and slowly tracked northwest in association with a supercell thunderstorm. The tornado produced patchy tree damage visible on high resolution satellite imagery with the most notable tree displacement and evident uproots occurring north of Brewster Road near a electrical transmission line corridor. This was collocated with a brief tornado debris signature on KLIX radar imagery during the time the tornado crossed this area. The TDS weakened thereafter and very limited patchy tree damage was visible on high resolution satellite imagery indicating the tornado weakened thereafter and dissipated before reaching Hwy 1085.

A sporadic damage path of minor tree damage associated with an EF-0 tornado that occurred near MS Hwy 15 in northeast Harrison County on October 28, 2020 was identified using high resolution satellite imagery. This was corroborated by collocation with a well-defined tornado vortex signature on both KLIX and KMOB radars as well as a trained weather spotter report of small limbs and tree debris as well as power flashes as this tornado crossed the highway.
Large tree branches were broken and small tree was uprooted by thunderstorm winds.

An EF1 tornado touched down just southwest of Fordsville Road east of Tylertown, MS. The worst damage damage was seen just northeast of the touchdown point with light damage to a roof and an area of tree damage with multiple uprooted trees. Light tree damage was noted along the path until it crossed into Marion County where the roof of a restaurant was damaged on Highway 98.
The KNEW ASOS at Lakefront Airport measured a thunderstorm wind gust of 44 mph or 38 knots.
Vehicles were stranded due to high water near Silo Drive in the Settlement at Willow Grove.
DOTD crews were barricading impassable roads on the western side of Zachary due to high water from heavy rainfall.
Water was overflowing ditches and encroaching onto homes along Lindsey Erin Lane near Albany.
A social media post showed a creek overflowing its bank near Percy Quin State Park. The water covered a bridge that crossed the creek and a gravel driveway by several feet.

A social media post showed widespread flooding along Highway 44, just north of Cazzie Cothern Road. The home was completely surrounded by water at least a few feet deep. Several vehicles appear to be flooded.
A social media post showed a picture of several cars flooded along Pine Street and Douglas Drive near Higgins Middle School. The water appeared to be a couple feet deep.
A social media post showed dozens of portable buildings flooded or floating along Highway Highway 48 near Union Church Road.

A 17-year-old male was swimming with friends near the jetties at Grand Isle Beach when he was pulled offshore by a rip current and submerged.  At approximately 2:11 PM CDT, the U.S. Coast Guard received a report from the Jefferson Parish Sheriff���s Office (JPSO) of a swimmer in distress about 500 yards from the jetties. Two JPSO deputies on scene initially maintained visual contact with the swimmer before losing sight of him.  The Coast Guard Sector New Orleans Command Center issued an Urgent Marine Information Broadcast and deployed a response boat from Coast Guard Station Grand Isle, along with an MH-60 Jayhawk helicopter from Coast Guard Air Station New Orleans. Search efforts by Coast Guard personnel along the shoreline were initially unsuccessful.  JPSO and local emergency medical services later located a body matching the swimmer���s description that had washed ashore. The individual was subsequently identified by the Jefferson Parish Coroner���s Office as 17-year-old Jordan Naquin of Houma, Louisiana.

The damage path of an EF-0 tornado was identified in extreme southwestern East Feliciana Parish, near Lindsay, LA. This tornado caused predominantly minor tree damage including evident displacement and damage of trees consistent with maximum estimated winds near 80 mph. The tornado tracked from King's View Circle through Highway 964 and Thompson Rd before evidently dissipating over open rural fields near the parish line. This damage path was closely located with a strong area of rotation on KHDC radar imagery.

An NWS storm survey team determined that an EF-1 tornado with peak winds of 90 mph embedded in a line of storms touched down along Highway 1 in far western Ascension Parish just after midnight on February 15th. Here, the tornado mainly snapped large branches and small tree trunks. The tornado continued eastward causing minor tree damage as it crossed Hwy 405 and the Mississippi River. More damage to large branches and tree tops was observed along River Rd north of Darrow. The tornado continued to move east-southeast over inaccessible areas until it reached Ruffin Martinez Rd and Highway 22. More large branches were snapped here as it continued moving to the east-southeast towards Walter Hill Rd. The tornado then crossed the Mississippi River a 2nd time and remained over either open fields or a refinery. The tornado reached peak intensity as it approached Highway 70 where it snapped a few tree trunks. The tornado then continued over the marsh east of Highway 70 where it likely lifted near the Ascension/St. James Parish line.

An NWS Storm Survey team determined that an EF-1 tornado with peak winds of 105 mph embedded in a line of storms touched down just north of the Ascension/Assumption Parish line shortly after midnight on February 15th. This tornado started by snapping large branches and uprooting a tree on Te Nom Landry Rd and Highway 308 south. It continued moving east-northeast over open fields until reaching the intersection of Highway 3089 and Highway 70. Here, the tornado strengthened to EF-1 intensity where a power pole and tree trunk were snapped. This tornado maintained intensity as it continued moving to the east-northeast where it snapped a series of powerlines off of Baxter Rd on the south side of the CF Industries complex. The tornado then started to intensify to peak intensity as it crossed into St. James Parish while moving through mainly open fields before it hit a series of powerlines in an open field, snapping 4 lines. It maintained strength as it crossed another open field along Badger Rd before snapping another series of powerlines along Highway 18. The tornado appeared to weaken as it continued to move east-northeast across the Mississippi River. When the tornado reached Highway 3125, it partially snapped/bent another powerline. The tornado then moved into the marsh north of Highway 3025 before reaching Highway 61 where it uprooted another tree. The last damage point for this tornado is along I-10 where it snapped more large branches.

An EF-1 tornado touched down along August Ln, just west of Polo Rd, where it damaged trees and a roof of a residence. It moved east along Polo Rd with sporadic tree damage. The heaviest tree damage occurred along Spirit of the Forest Ln and River Trace Rd where more than a dozen very large trees were uprooted or snapped. Periodic tree and large limb damage occurred along the remainder of the path until the tornado lifted in the Merrywood Estates subdivision. Path length was 9.3 miles. Max width was 75 yards. Estimated maximum winds around 95 mph.

An NWS ground survey confirmed an EF-0 tornado with maximum sustained winds estimated near 85 mph tracked across parts of southwest and central Washington Parish, south of Franklinton, LA. This tornado began near Sam Smith Rd where it snapped a rotted large hardwood tree. Additional tree debris and minor damage to skirting of a manufactured home was noted nearby. The tornado continued east-northeast where more abundant tree damage was identified including snaps of smaller tree trunks and branches along Daniels Rd, west of LA Hwy 25. This was where the tornado appeared to be at its strongest and widest, spanning about 75 yards wide. The tornado continued across the Bogue Chitto River, and additional minor tree damage was found by the survey team along LA Hwy 16, Tullos Rd, and Gene Williams Rd. Near Lee Rd and Thigpen Rd was where the last area of more concentrated minor tree damage was noted and this was the estimated end point of this tornado damage path. No additional damage was identified on Moore Rd nor LA Hwy 439, however, minor sporadic tree damage did continue farther east, north of Bogalusa, LA.

An NWS storm survey team confirmed an EF-0 with peak winds of 85 mph touched down on the southern side of Thibodaux at 12:45am on February 15th. An trailer RV was partially flipped off of Talbot Ave as the tornado moved to the east-southeast. The tornado then reach peak strength as it impacted Tabernacle Pentecostal Church. Here, the tornado lifted a significant portion of the roof of the church, displacing it to the east. The wood framing of the roofing had evidence of rotting, so the lower bound for that damage was used in this case. The tornado slightly weakened as it moved east-southeast where minimal damage was found until it reached Percy Brown Rd where multiple large branches were snapped along it. The tornado remained very weak as it continued to the east-southeast where the next notable damage came on Crossing North St where a backyard awning was uplifted. As the tornado moved to the east-northeast, vegetation damage was noted on high-resolution imagery north of Rousseau where the tornado appeared to have lifted though additional analysis will be needed to determine the end point over inaccessible areas.

An EF-1 tornado touched down along Ancil Cox Road on the southwest side of Centreville near Griffin Lane. A few trees were downed here, with at least one of them taking down a powerline. The tornado tracked northeast, generally paralleling Ancil Cox Road until reaching the intersection with Old Highway 33. The most significant damage occurred near this intersection, where approximately a dozen trees were uprooted or snapped which supports the 90 mph wind rating. Beyond this point, the tornado continued northeastward producing sporadic tree and limb damage along its path. The final accessible point of the tornado���s track was near Centerville Academy. Minor damage was observed on campus, including a downed light pole, partial roof uplift on a metal building, and a baseball pitching backstop that was thrown approximately 250 feet into a chain-link fence. The tornado continued northeast beyond Lower Centreville Rd where additional minor tree damage was identified. The tornado evidently lifted over inaccessible areas to the survey team prior to reaching Hwy 48.

An NWS storm survey with additional support from a local storm report has confirmed an EF-1 tornado occurred west of Liberty, MS in Amite County. This tornado began near Berwick Cassels and Smylie Rd where minor tree damage was identified. Additional patches of increasingly more notable tree damage as wide as 175 yards occurred as the tornado tracked northeast along Smylie Rd. The tornado reached peak intensity with maximum sustained winds near 100 mph as it approached Enterprise Rd and Lower Liberty Gloster Rd where it snapped tree trunks and uprooted numerous trees. A manufactured observed minor roof damage. More tree damage from this tornado was identified where it crossed MS Hwy 24, moving northeast. A local storm report identified additional notable tree damage with a few uprooted/snapped medium to large pine trees near Rattlesnake Ln. This tornado evidently lifted near the Amite River just before reaching Old 24 Compromise Rd.

An EF-1 tornado with peak winds of 100 mph tracked north of Peoria, MS in Amite County. The tornado began near Patterson Rd where minor tree damage was identified. This minor tree damage continued northeast becoming gradually more severe as the tornado approached Peoria Rd. Dozens of trees were snapped and uprooted near and northeast of Peoria Rd as the tornado reached its peak intensity and a width of 200 yards. The tornado tracked northeast, crossing Highway 24 and East Fork Rd. Numerous trees were snapped and uprooted along this portion of the path. Additional minor tree damage was identified beyond East Fork Rd and Pray Rd on high resolution satellite imagery as the tornado evidently weakened. Patches of tree damage continued through Bass, Barron, Brown, and Thompson roads. Another brief swath of heavier tree damage occurred north of Thompson Rd as the tornado briefly reached a second peak at EF-1 intensity. The tornado weakened again and is estimated to have lifted after crossing Tangipahoa Rd and Hwy 570 where tree damage became too sparse to be considered a coherent track.

An EF-0 tornado with maximum sustained winds estimated near 80 mph touched down near US Hwy 98 in far northeast Amite County, MS causing minor tree damage and removing a few metal panels from an outbuilding. The tornado continued northeast into Pike County where additional minor tree damage was found on Kenna Rd. This tornado continued northeast into Lincoln County, MS where it strengthened into a large, strong EF-1 tornado with maximum sustained winds near 110 mph southwest of Norfield, MS in NWS Jackson's area.

The track of an EF-0 tornado was identified via high resolution satellite imagery in association with a quick spin-up circulation within a line of storms. This tornado evidently damaged and/or displaced trees along mainly inaccessible areas near South Valley Rd and Kennedy Creek in Pearl River County, MS. The damage path peaked at approximately 70 yards wide and apparently ended after crossing Sun Valley Acres Rd, prior to reaching John Amacker Rd.

An EF-1 tornado quickly spun up along a line of strong thunderstorms near Liverpool LA, south of LA 1043. This tornado caused predominantly uprooted and snapped tree damage as it tracked southeast. It began to track more east-southeast as it exited St Helena Parish and entered Tangipahoa Parish near LA 10 just west of I-55. Peak intensity was 95 mph and max width was 200 yards.

An EF-1 tornado entered Tangipahoa Parish from St Helena Parish a couple miles west of I-55 just north of LA 10. A few trees were snapped and uprooted by the tornado along the interstate before dissipating.

A 65 MPH EF0 tornado touched down north of Albany, LA and tracked southeast. The damage was large branches and tree debris along the line that also lines up with the radar signature. The tornado exited Livingston Parish and entered Tangipahoa Parish just west of Kinchen Road about one half mile south of Highway 442.

A 65 MPH EF0 tornado entered Tangipahoa Parish from Livingston Parish just west of  Kinchen Road about one half mile south of Highway 442. The damage was large branches and tree debris along the line that also lines up with the radar signature. The tornado lifted after reaching Woodhaven Road.

An EF-0 tornado with maximum sustained winds of 85 mph rapidly developed along a line of thunderstorms near Hwy 1047 and Deer Creek Rd. Minor tree damage was noted in this portion of the track. The tornado exited St Helena Parish and entered Tangipahoa Parish 1 mile north of Highway 1048.

An EF-0 tornado with maximum sustained winds of 85 mph rapidly developed along a line of thunderstorms, near the Tangipahoa and St. Helena Parish border. As it cross the parish line 1 mile north of Highway 1048 into a solar farm where a weak tornado debris signature became evident on KHDC. Only minor tree damage was evident along this section of Interstate 55. Additional tree damage including uproots and snapped tree tops were evident between I-55 and Hwy 51 which was collocated with a stronger tornado debris signature on KHDC. The tornado likely peaked in strength and size in this area. Thereafter, the tornado crossed the Tangipahoa River and began moving east-southeast toward LA Hwy 10. The tornado caused mostly uprooted trees and snapped large limbs off of trees along LA Hwy 10 before it dissipated just east of LA 1054.

A EF-0 tornado with a maximum wind speed of 65 mph touched down just east of Loranger. This was determined via a ground survey point and minor tree damage evident on high resolution satellite imagery. This track was collocated with a weak tornado debris signature evident on radar imagery from nearby KHDC.

An EF-1 tornado with peak winds of 95 mph and max width of 200 yards rapidly developed within a strong line of thunderstorms southeast of Lewiston, LA along LA 38. This tornado predominantly caused minor tree damage as it tracked southeastward, maintaining EF-0 intensity as it exited Tangipahoa Parish and entered Washington Parish just northwest of the intersection of LA 450 and LA 1057.

An EF-1 tornado with peak winds of 95 mph and max width of 200 yards entered Washington Parish from Tangipahoa Parish just northwest of the intersection of LA 1057 and LA 450. The tornado strengthened, uprooting trees and snapping large branches and the tops of trunks as it reached LA Hwy 10 and moved into Sylvest Rd. Additional tree damage was identified downstream of the surveyed end point of this tornado via high resolution satellite imagery which evidently dissipated prior to it reaching LA Hwy 16, west of Franklinton.

An EF-1 tornado quickly spun up along a line of strong thunderstorms just east of Franklinton Louisiana. The tornado tracked southeastward through southern areas of Franklinton, causing moderate roof damage to a Floral Shop and damaging a business sign. As it crossed LA 16 it caused minor roof damage to homes and an apartment building while also causing a couple trees to fall on a home and shed. After the tornado crossed south of LA 1072 it caused moderate damage to a forecast, snapping about 40-50 small pine trees. This was the peak intensity of the tornado which was 105 mph. This tornado caused several uprooted and snapped trees along its path. Finally the tornado tracked further southeast, before dissipating east of LA 1072 north of Fussell Road.

An EF-0 tornado with peak wind of 80 mph and max width of 50 yards rapidly developed within a line of storms near Blond, LA in St. Tammany Parish. This tornado predominantly uprooted and damaged tree branches and rotten trunks as it tracked from Allison Rd east-southeast through LA Hwy 40 before dissipating near Lee Road Junior High School.

An EF-0 tornado with peak winds 75 mph and max width of 50 yards rapidly developed within a line of storms subsequently after the dissipation of an EF-0 tornado to its southwest. This tornado caused minor tree damage along a defined path from a private residence west of LA Hwy 1082 and Elderberry Ln east-southeast to LA Hwy 1083 near Oalmann Rd.

The damage path of an EF-0 tornado with estimated peak winds near 85 mph and max width was identified on high resolution satellite imagery in northeast Wilkinson County, just south of Perrytown, MS. Evident damage and displacement to trees were identified near Turkey Creek Rd which extended to the east-southeast through to Tom Crum Rd which was closely collocated to a strong area of rotation on KHDC. The majority of this damage path was inaccessible to ground survey and thus is rated via identifiable damage via satellite.

The damage path of an EF-1 tornado with maximum sustained winds of 90 mph and max width of 200 yards was identified via high resolution satellite imagery in northwest Amite County, north of Gloster, MS. This tornado caused damage and displacement to several trees including a swath west of Hwy 33 concurrent with an EF-1. Additional tree damage was identified along Hwy 33 near Homochitto Rd. This was corroborated by EM report of tree damage north of Gloster which also was collocated with a strong area of rotation on KHDC radar.

The damage path of an EF-0 tornado with maximum sustained winds near 85 mph and peak width of 150 yards was identified on high resolution satellite imagery in rural Amite County, north of Liberty, MS. Damage to tree tops were identified west of Pecan Rd. A focused path of damaged and displaced trees continued east-southeast through Meadville and Freeman Rd. The tornado evidently lifted after crossing Hwy 569, prior to reaching Newman Rd where no other damage could be identified. This damage path was collocated with a strong area of rotation of KHDC radar imagery.

A strong EF-1 tornado touched down south of Hwy 570 near Moak Rd in Pike County, MS. This tornado rapidly strengthened and grew in size as it tracked to the east-northeast causing destruction of a wood frame farm outbuilding and increasingly significant treefall as it crossed Kodiak Ln and Magnolia Pisgah Rd. While there was a high proportion of treefall associated with this tornado in this area, a significant portion was due to uprooted trees from soft soils due to recent heavy rainfall. As such, maximum sustained winds were estimated near 110 mph despite the heavy deforestation. This level of heavy deforestation spanning approximately 375 yards wide at peak width continued across Hwy 570 to Dye Ln where tree damage rapidly became less significant. It's estimated that this tornado rapidly lifted as it crossed Magee Rd.

An EF-1 tornado with peak estimated winds near 105 mph and max width of 300 yards touched down near Johnston Chapel Rd. A broadly defined area of uprooted and damaged trees was identified via high resolution satellite imagery near the beginning of this path which continued east-southeast across Old Brookhaven Rd and Interstate 55. This damage was corroborated by a storm report with pictures of numerous uprooted trees near Chapel Dr. The tornado began to strengthen and increase in size with complex multi-vortex behaviors evident according to the damage path present after crossing I-55. Numerous trees were snapped and uprooted along US Hwy 51, Rollingwood Drive, and Johnston Station Rd. Additional tree damage was surveyed near Lakeside Drive on Southwest Mississippi Community College campus. The tornado continued east destroying a cinderblock dugout at North Pike High School. More tree damage was also identified on Barrett Drive and Jaguar Trail. Scattered pockets of wind damage were evident via ground survey across Barnett Rd and L.D. White Rd, but the most cohesive damage points representative of a tornado damage path were evident to the southeast as the multi-vortex tornado continued to produce patches and swaths of tree damage on high resolution satellite imagery near Hwy 570 and and River Ridge Rd. The tornado damage path evidently became incoherent after crossing River Ridge Rd and it's estimated the tornado lifted prior to reaching Hwy 44.

An EF-1 tornado with peak winds of 90 mph and width of 175 yards rapidly developed along Hwy 570, northwest of McComb, MS on the evening of March 11th. This tornado damage path was distinctly different to the predecessor tornado along Hwy 570 as most of the confluent damage was directed southeast and east as the KHDC velocity signature denoted the strong rotation center of this tornado diving southeastward along the highway. This tornado uprooted several trees, snapped the tops of tree trunks, tossed a golf cart approximately 70 yards, and caused minor roof damage to a couple homes as it tracked along the highway. Additional tree damage was near Delaware Avenue where confluence of damage direction was identified. These damage path characteristics are subject to change.

An EF-1 tornado with peak winds of 95 mph touched down just north of the intersection of Ohio Ave. and Polk St. in Gulfport. The tornado quickly tracked to the south causing sporadic tree damage that consisted primarily of large tree limbs being blown off of trees as tracked southward between Wisconsin Ave. and West Railroad Ave. The tornado continued south-southeast across US Hwy 49 with visible damage observed to commercial businesses in this area. Large branches and snapped trees were observed between 34th St. and 28th St. At the intersection of 28th St. and 22nd Ave. two metal buildings had their garage doors blown out as the tornado continued south-southeast. At the intersection of Pass Road and 22nd Ave. a large hardwood tree was completely uprooted. The tornado then crossed Pass Road and produced additional tree damage in the form of large branches and a few snapped trees. The snapped trees were either dead and diseased, so the windspeed was lowered to 90 mph to account for this. As the tornado crossed the railroad track, minor damage to a home in the form of a few removed shingles was observed on 3rd St. The tornado then moved offshore near the intersection of Beach Blvd. and Pratt Ave.

Similar damage occurred as the tornado tracked to the southeast across Pass Road and 28th Street. The tornado continued to the southeast and reached peak intensity of 90 mph near the intersection of 5th Avenue and 25th Street where a few trees were snapped. One hardwood tree was hollow inside and the other snap was very high. Numerous large branches were also removed from several trees near this intersection. The tornado then continued to the southeast crossing Gulf Avenue near 24th Street producing sporadic tree damage. The tornado then crossed the railroad just west of Hewes St. where additional large branches were removed from several trees all the way to Beach Blvd. Numerous trees were observed to have lost large branches between Roberts Ave. and Centennial Plaza on Beach Blvd.

A thunderstorm produced heavy rainfall of two to three inches in a short period of time resulting in widespread street flooding in areas of Houma. In addition, a number of homes experienced minor flooding, primarily in the Broadmoor subdivision.

Tropical Storm Edouard formed over the north central Gulf of Mexico on the afternoon of August 3rd. Edouard moved east northeast offshore the south Louisiana coastline before making landfall on the upper Texas Coast on Tuesday August 5th. The affect on the southeast Louisiana were minimal and confined to the coastal areas west of the Mississippi River. Tropical storm force winds, primarily in gusts, occurred along the coast. Tides were generally 1 to 3 feet above normal with a few low lying roadways having minor flooding. Lowest pressure recorded was 1009.2 mb at the LUMCON facility at Cocodrie. Maximum sustained winds at the LUMCON-Tambour Bay site were 34 knots and a peak wind of 38 knots. At the LUMCON-Cocodrie facility a wind gust of 34 knots was observed.  A maximum storm tide of 3.2 feet NAVD88 was observed at the LUMCON Cocodrie site. Storm total rainfall was less than an inch. Maximum storm total rainfall was 0.86 inches at the LSU Ag Station near Houma.

Storm surge of 1 to 3 feet above normal was experienced along the southeast Louisiana coast as Tropical Storm Edouard moved across the northern Gulf of Mexico. Minimal impact was felt along the coast with only minor flooding of a few coastal roadways. Maximum storm tide was 3.2 feet recorded at the LUMCON-Cocodrie facility.

events.event_narrative: Thunderstorm winds knocked down numerous trees and power lines throughout the city. A tree fell on a house on Stanford Avenue. Significant tree damage occurred around the Louisiana State University campus and in the Southdowns area. Scattered commercial signs along Perkins Road were blown down. Significant structural damage occurred to the Louisiana State University football indoor facility and several other buildings had roof damage. Damage at the LSU campus was estimated around four million dollars. A survey crew estimated sustained winds speeds near 80 mph. The Baton Rouge ASOS equipment at Baton Rouge Ryan Field Airport located north of the worst damage recorded at 67 mph wind gust. Entergy Louisiana reported that more than 14,600 of their customers were without power in East Baton Rouge Parish.

Numerous power poles were knocked down with multiple electrical transformers blown off poles. Also, scattered trees were knocked down and a roof was ripped off of a house along Antonio Road near Highway 1.

Widespread tree and power line damage due to thunderstorm winds was observed across Livingston Parish. Some of the worst daamge was along State Highway 1020 where power lines and trees blocked the road. Also, more concentrated tree and power line damage was reported along Highway 447 south of Interstate 12 and along Hood Road south of Walker.

A National Weather Service ground storm survey indicated a tornado path of approximately three quarters of a mile long and 50 yards wide in the vicinity of School Road and Highway 40. Seven homes were damaged, one mobile home was destroyed, and one trailer heavily damaged. One minor injury was reported. Several large trees were uprooted and broken off. The maximum estimated wind speeds associated with this tornado were in the 100 to 110 mph range.
A power pole was knocked down along Highway 40 near Loranger.

A very weak tornado briefly touched down in the Springhill subdivision. The tornado was only about 25 yards wide with a path length of approximately 250 yards. The tornado resulted in minor tree damage and caused yard items to be blown around. The estimated wind speed associated with this tornado was around 65 mph.
Numerous trees were blown down and there were power outages along Highway 24 near Woodville.
Thunderstorm winds were knocked down trees along Interstate 59 around mile marker 10 near Carriere. Also, power outages were reported around Picayune.
A few trees were blown down along Lower Bay Road just to the west southwest of Waveland.

A weak tornado briefly touched down causing damage around Tucker Street and 8th Street and on Taylor Street. Pacagoula High School experienced light damage when the scoreboard on the football field was blown down and numerous sections of fence were knocked down with debris littering the field. Traffic lights around the area were knocked down and several trees were blown down. Maximum winds associated with this tornado were estimated around 75 mph with a path length around 250 yards and a maximum width of 50 yards.
Nickel size hail was observed.
Thunderstorm winds destroyed one trailer and knocked two trailers off of their blocks. Several tree limbs were knocked down and a tree fell on a house.
Thunderstorm winds blew down trees at Highway 43 and Leetown Road.

A tornado touched down in the St. Amant community. One house was moved off of its foundation and had its roof blown off.  A large metal commercial building was heavily damaged. Emergency management officials reported that one structure was destroyed, 10 structures received severe damage, and 20 structures moderate damage. The path length of the tornado was approximately 1.75 miles and the path width 50 yards.

A National Weather Service storm survey indicated that a weak tornado briefly touched down just west of Kilian along Miller Road. Numerous trees were uprooted, a trailer was overturned, and a barn received minor damage.
A tornado ripped a 200 foot section of roofing material off of a school, removed the roof of a mobile home, and knocked down or snapped numerous trees.
Trees were blown down in Pierre Part.
Thunderstorm winds damaged two trailers on Highway 1010. One trailer had its roof ripped off and another trailer was blown over on its side.
One inch diamater hail was reported along U.S. Highway 98.
The awning of a gas station on North Broadway was blown over.
Heavy rain caused water to enter a home in McComb.

A National Weather Service storm survey indicated that a tornado traveled along a 7 mile long path in Hancock County. The tornado caused substantial damage to the roof of a church on Highway 603 and to a large outbuilding south of Necaise. The debris from large trees blocked Highway 603, Highway 43, and Highway 53.
A National Weather Service storm survey indicated that a tornado briefly touched down just north of Hickory. The tornado caused substantial roof damage to 3 homes near Highway 41.
Trees were knocked down in eastern Orleans parish along Highway 11 in Irish Bayou.
A waterspout was reported in eastern Lake Pontchartrain near the Interstate 10 Twinspan Bridge.
Thunderstorm winds knocked down numerous trees in southern sections of the county which blocked some roads.
Several trees were blown down on streets in the city of McComb.
Several roads were washed out in the southern part of the county.
Portions of U.S. Highway 90 around Bay St. Louis and Waveland were flooded due to heavy rainfall.

Major flooding due to heavy rain affected portions of Harrison County. The cities which experienced the worst flooding were Gulfport, Biloxi, D'Iberville, and Long Beach. At least 100 roads were impacted by flooding with numerous cars under water near the entrance to Interstate 10 off of the Interstate 110 loop. Around 200 homes flooded with most having 12 inches or less of water in them. A 36 year old man drowned in D'Iberville when he drove into a flooded drainage ditch.
Heavy rain caused the flooding of numerous roadways around the county and it was estimated that over 150 homes flooded.
Several roads were closed due to high water around Dexter and two bridges were washed out.
Several roads were closed around Pike County due to high water.
Numerous roadways across the parish were impacted by high water due to heavy rain.
Widespread and severe flooding occurred in many areas of Terrebonne Parish. It was estimated that around 240 homes and businesses were flooded. Numerous roads around the parish were flooded.

Widespread and severe flooding occurred in areas of Lafourche Parish due to heavy rain. It was estimated that around 150 homes and businesses flooded. Most of the flooded structures had 2 to 5 inches of water in them; however, a few had up to 18 inches of water. Lockport had 8 businesses, 51 homes, and some apartment complexes flooded. Bayou blue had 25 homes flooded. Mathews had 20 homes flooded.
Many streets were flooded due to heavy rain and numerous vehicles were under water.
Some homes and a number of vehicles were flooded due to heavy rain.
Coastal flooding was observed outside the levee system at Larose where a shipyard was under 2 feet of water.
Heavy rainfall flooded a number of roadways and vehicles around Chalmette.
Coastal flooding was observed on Beach Boulevard near Waveland.
Heavy rainfall flooded numerous roadways and some homes and vehicles on the Westbank of Jefferson Parish.
Heavy rainfall resulted in major street flooding around Destrehan, Luling, and St. Rose.

EF0 tornado confirmed by NWS storm survey. Damage to a mobile home was in Lucy on River Road. There were no injuries outside of cuts from flying debris. Tornado path was 100 yards long and 50 feet wide.
Trees were blown down in the city of Gretna.
Over 2.5 inches of rain between 8 am and 10 am at City Hall. Numerous roads were reported to be impassible. Cars were floating in several intersections.
Trees and power lines down with power outages in the parish.
A light pole was blown down.
A small tree was downed and nickel size hail covered the ground in Robinwood Forest Subdivision.
Wind damage to a roof and broken window. Pea size hail also.
Quarter size hail reported in Burns and Southwood communities.
Thunderstorm winds downed trees and left 4800 customers without power.
Emergency Manager reported 1 mobile home with severe roof damage and 3 mobile homes with minor roof damage.
Quarter size hail reported at Stennis Space Center.
Golf ball size hail reported at Stennis Space Center.
Golf ball size hail reported in Diamondhead.
Roof peeled back on metal commercial building near Highway 43 and Highway 603.
Quarter size hail reported in St. Martin.
A National Data Buoy Center employee reported metal storage shed and fence blown down in St. Martin.
Power and cable out due to thunderstorm winds in Lacombe.

An 8 inch diameter tree downed by strong winds.
Observer at KNBG...NAS New Orleans...reported quarter size hail.
Water covering Highway 23.
Winds estimated at 60 mph in Mandeville.
Five power poles blown down in south end of Gramercy along Highway 641.
Quarter size hail reported just east of the Interstate 10 and 12 split by a family member of a NWS employee.
Public report relayed by NWS employee.

An eight year old boy from Columbus, Mississippi was fatally injured by lightning at a family gathering. The child was standing near a tree when the tree was struck by lightning from a thunderstorm. No rain was occurring at the time of the lightning strike. The boy was admitted to the hospital, and died on June 2.
Weather observer at New Orleans International Airport reported a brief waterspout over Lake Pontchartrain.
Residents of Forest Brook and Monterrey subdivisions reporting water in streets and approaching homes.
Power lines were downed on Omega Drive. Report was relayed by emergency manager. Time of report based on radar and surface observations.
Wind damage and downed power poles were reported on Broad Street in New Orleans.
Power lines and trees down at Haas Road and Fremaux Avenue in Slidell.

A National Weather Service team has surveyed the damage and concluded that it was caused by a microburst. Wind speeds were estimated at 70 to 80 mph. Widespread small limb damage was noted as well as a few medium to large size trees downed. Damage was confined to an area bounded by Patricia St. to the north...Alexander St. to the west...Rowley St. to the east and St. Bernard Highway to the south.
A few trees were twisted and knocked down near Pine.
Several trees down in various locations around Slidell. Reported by Slidell Police Department.
Lightning triggered a fire at a condominium in Baton Rouge.
A 38 knot wind gust was measured at Lakefront Airport at 2104Z.
A few trees were blown down on French Town Road. Report came front East Baton Rouge Fire Communications.
A few trees were reported blown down on Highway 64. Report came from East Baton Rouge Fire Communications.
Minor coastal flooding was reported along Beach Boulevard and other roads near Waveland Marina. The tide gage at Wavelend reached 3.9 ft MLLW, about 2 feet above normal levelsl.
Water on Kiln-Delisle Road with water reported up to window level on vehicles.
The tin roof of a maintenance shed was torn off, and three trees were blown down at Oak Alley Plantation. Report was from The L'Observateur newspaper in Laplace.
Lightning caused a tree to fall onto a neighbor's home in Mandeville. Three rooms in the home were damaged.
Wind and lightning from thunderstorms knocked down several trees that fell across power lines producing a 12 hour power outage in the New Roads area.

A waterspout was observed over Lake Pontchartrain near the Causeway.

A weak tornado touched down in the 1500 block of Prentiss Avenue. A few shingles were blown off a roof. Several trees were knocked down and a garbage can was blown into electrical wires. Report was from New Orleans PD.
A picture of a waterspout over Lake Pontchartrain was received from a spotter located near the Bonnabel Boat Launch.
NOAA C-Man station at Shell Beach - SHBL1 - reported 30 knot sustained winds and a gust to 45 knots.
Thunderstorm winds knocked down several trees in the Kenner area.

Heavy rain, possibly as much as 8 inches in 90 minutes, produced flooding of streets and approximately 110 homes in the parish. The water in homes was generally several inches in depth. Media reports indicated around 20 homes were affected in the Lynndale subdivision and 15 homes in Brusly.
Lightning triggered a fire that destroyed a home in the Bayou Blue area.
Winds from a thunderstorm blew down six trees on Buford Creel Road.
Six inches of rain caused wash outs on  several roads and near bridges in northern Washington Parish. More than 20 roads and bridges were damaged in the parish.
A 40 year old man died due to heat stroke while fishing in Delacroix. Heat index values were near 110 degrees in the area at the time.

A 48 year old construction worker collapsed and died while working on a highway construction project. Jackson County coroner classified the fatality as heat related with the cause of death as hyperthermia.

NOAA gage on Lake Pontchartrain at New Canal measured a wind gust of 36 knots.
New Orleans Lakefront Airport measured a wind gust of 39 knots.
Trees were downed by thunderstorm winds on Highway 444 between Highway 63 and Bull Run Road.
A 41 knot wind gust was measured at Bay Waveland Yacht Club.
A waterspout was observed near the intersection of Highway 90 and 41st Street in Gulfport.
Water intruded into the first floor of an apartment comlex in southeast Metairie near Ochsner Medical Center. There were also several flooded streets in Bridge City.
The Sheriff's Office reported trees down on several roads in the county.
A 48 mph wind gust was measured at the Highway 90 Bridge Marina.
A trained spotter reported that a house was taking on water on Napoleon Street in New Roads.

Pointe Coupee Law Enforcement reported ongoing street flooding and water in homes along several local streets, including New Roads Street...Louisiana Street...Richey Street...Janis Street and Berthier Street.
Pointe Coupee Law Enforcement reported a home on fire on Cooks Landing Drive in Ventress due to lightning.
Louisiana Highway 10 was flooded near Morganza.
Low water bridges were flooded in rural areas near St. Francisville.
WCYM6 NOS station reported a wind gust to 34 knots.
Two boats doing surveillance near the mouth of the Pearl River sighted a strong waterspout.

events.event_narrative: A wind gust of 35 knots was reported at Southwest Pass.
A few trees were reported down with one onto a shed and another onto a carport. Report was relayed by a Baton Rouge TV station. Event time was estimated by radar.
Seven inches of rain produced flooding of five homes in Des Allemands, Bayou Gauche, Boutte and Paradis.
Two businesses were flooded near Jefferson Highway and Metairie Road.
Seven roads in Jefferson Parish buckled due to heat.
Thunderstorm winds flipped one airplane. An awning was torn from the terminal building which ripped off an attic vent and left a hole in the roof. This allowed rain water to damage a meeting room.
Heavy rain flooded Wooddale Avenue with flood water entering a food market.
Heavy rain produced flooding in central and southern portions of Lafourche Parish. Several roads were closed by the flooding.
Lightning caused electrical damage to a home, and knocked down a tree which fell onto an automobile and a home in Baker.
Lightning sparked a fire that caused major damage to the second story of a home in Dularge.
Lightning downed several trees and triggered power outages in Hammond, and between Tickfaw and Independence.
Thunderstorms produced street flooding in several areas of Hammond and surrounding portions of Tangipahoa Parish.
Several reports of street flooding were received in Baton Rouge.
A waterspout was observed by a trained spotter over northern Lake Pontchartrain southeast of Mandeville.

The Harrison County Coroner stated that two deaths in a mobile home on Smith Road near Canal Road were caused by heat stroke. High temperatures at Gulfport Airport, approximately 3 miles away, were between 98 and 102 degrees from July 29 through August 2. Bodies were discovered on August 4, but deaths occurred several days prior to that. Date of deaths was estimated.
Five inches of rain from the remnants of Tropical Depression Five flooded yards and approached homes near Hammond High School east of Hammond.
Quarter size hail was reported on Highway 955.
A few trees were reported downed on Highway 955.
A Sheriffs Office Deputy reported nickel size hail near Tunica.
Quarter to golfball size hail covered the ground northwest of Covington.
Hail measured slightly larger than a quarter northwest of Covington.
A waterspout was observed 5 miles south of Gautier. The waterspout lifted before reaching land.
Thunderstorm wind gusts blew down a tree and knocked out power to homes near Landon Road and Coleman Road in northern Gulfport.
Several trees were reported down near the intersection of Carr Bridge Road and Blackwell Farm Road.
Culverts were washed out on several rural roadways in the Fort Adams area.
Flooding was reported on US Highway 61 in the Doloroso area.
Strong thunderstorm winds destroyed a shed and blew a shutter off a home on Lower Glading Road southwest of McComb.

Television broadcast media in Baton Rouge reported and Baker Police Department confirmed minor damage from a tornado that briefly touched down and blew tin off a roof. Photos and video confirmed a condensation funnel that reached within 20 to 50 feet of the ground. Also received a report of corrugated metal peeled off a lumber storage building in the same area.
A thunderstorm produced heavy rain in Metairie causing street flooding including on Causeway Blvd.

Thunderstorm winds estimated at 70 mph blew the roof off of a trailer in the Chackbay area.
Thunderstorm winds knocked down a telephone pole on Highway 1 near Lockport.

Thunderstorm winds knocked several trees down in the Apache Drive area, as well as near Sinclair and Louisiana Avenues. Wind also blew down a tree onto a house. Power was knocked out to about 2500 customers in the McComb area.
A wind gust of 41 knots was measured at Lakefront Airport.
Thunderstorm winds blew down a tree in Port Sulphur.
NOAA CMAN station SHBL1 at Shell Beach measured a wind gust of 35 knots.
NWS wind gage at mid Lake Pontchartrain recorded a wind gust of 36 knots.

Delayed report from Stennis security of a sighted waterspout on the service canal. The waterspout moved onshore briefly before lifting. Minor shingle damage was done to one structure.
AWOS at Stennis Space Center (KHSA) reported a measured peak gust of 50 knots.
Thunderstorm winds knocked down several trees in the Fort Adams area. Time of event estimated based on radar.
Thunderstorm winds knocked down trees in the Dolorosa area. Time of the event was estimated.
Thunderstorm winds blew several trees down near the intersection of Louisiana Highway 421 and Whitestown Road. Time of event estimated.
Sporadic tree and limb damage. Maximum wind speed estimated at 65 mph.
A 30 foot power pole was snapped after a tree fell on it in Mandeville. The report was made to the New Orleans Times Picayune via Cleco Power Company.
A main transmission line was blown down near the Central Business District. Interstate 10 was closed at Chef Menteur Highway due to power lines down on the Interstate.
A wind gust to 42 mph was measured at mid Lake Pontchartrain.
Lakefront Airport ASOS recorded a 39 mph wind gust.
The CMAN station near Waveland Yacht Club (WYCM6) measured a wind gust of 35.9 knots.
Thunderstorm winds overturned a trampoline and damaged some shingles on the roof of one home. Pea size hail was also reported.

Sheriff's Office reported trees down in Clinton.
