events.event_narrative: Spotter reported icing of Interstate 12 overpasses at the Pumpkin Center and Albany exits.

Interstate 10 between Exit 177...Highway 30 and Exit 182...Highway 22 closed in both directions due to roadway completely coated in ice. Reported on the Louisiana Department of Transportation and Development web site.
Minor icing on elevated surfaces, trees and bushes in Albany.
A 15 vehicle pileup on Interstate 55 near Manchac was caused by roadway icing due to freezing rain.
Bridges began icing over in Pike County.
Bridges began icing over in Amite County.
Ice accumulating on elevated objects, but not road surfaces.
Light glaze on trees and power lines in St. Francisville.
Objects being to ice over in New Roads.
U.S. 190 Bridge at Krotz Springs between Pointe Coupee Parish and St. Landry Parish icing over.
Light icing still occurring on cars and trees. Very light icing on bridges.
Icing impacting bridges in Liberty and Gloster. Ice accumulating on power lines and trees.
Icing occurring on bridges in Centreville. Ice accumulating on cars and other metal objects.
Highway 98 bridge closed in McComb due to ice. Ice accumulating on cars and other metal objects. Accumulation also beginning to be observed on trees and power lines.
Parish-wide observations of icing on cars, guardrails and other metal objects.
Icing on bridges in the county resulted in 7 traffic accidents.

Estimated 1/4 to 1/2 inch of ice accumulated overnight, causing power outages in two different parts of the county. Several tree branches fell between Pond and Pickneyville. Six cars skidded off of Highway 61 north of Woodville.
Estimated one quarter inch of ice accumulated overnight countywide. Icing observed on several bridges across the county with seven auto accidents reported due to icy roads.
Icing on Interstate 10 near Ramah led to a multi-car traffic accident that temporarily closed the Interstate, and caused one fatality. Light icing was also observed on bridges in Grosse Tete.

Estimated one quarter inch of ice accumulated overnight north of the Morganza Spillway. A couple of small trees and treetops down in that area, but no power outages. Temporary bridge closings occured during the morning hours due to icing.

Estimated one quarter inch of ice accumulated overnight. Highway 19 bridges in Slaughter were temporarily closed due to icing during the morning hours. One quarter inch of ice accumulated on cars and other metal objects.
Estimated one quarter inch of ice accumulated overnight on cars and other metal objects in the Kentwood area. No reports of accumulations on bridges or roadways.
The Cooperative observer near Pontchatoula measured 6.1 inches of rain between 1600CST and 1930CST.

A few roads in eastern portions of Hammond, including Old Covington Highway and Highway 190 East had water across them.  Several roads were flooded between the Hammond area and Pontchatoula. A few other roads were closed due to high water.
The LSU Agcenter in Hammond recorded 4.34 inches of rain since 1500CST.
A report was received from a resident that their trampoline was picked up above the roofline of their home and tossed into another yard. Tree limbs were also reported down.
A 59 mph wind gust was measured by the LSU Ag Station at Ben Hur.
A downed tree was blocking Highway 42 near Port Vincent. A photograph of the damage was forwarded to the National Weather Service by broadcast media. Possible tornado.
Power lines were reported down in Schriever from a possible tornado.

The Jefferson Parish Emergency Manager reported damage between 4th Street and Highway 90 on Garden Road. A wooden structure was damaged, telephone and power poles were reported down. A trampoline was thrown 200 feet. Damage was also reported at the corner of Ames Boulevard and 4th Street. Power lines were downed, roof damage occurred to one business with debris strewn across the area with standing water in the streets. A funnel cloud and possible tornado were spotted in the area at the time.
Roof damage was reported to trailers in the Lafitte area by emergency management and fire department personnel. Possible tornado. Time of the event was estimated by radar.
Public reports were received of small tree limbs down, as well as minor street flooding in the Terrytown area.
New Orleans International Airport reported 2.21 inches of rain between 1300CST and 1345CST.
A waterspout was sighted south of the Silver Slipper Casino moving to the east-northeast.
The Iberville Parish Emergency Manager reported roof damage to one residence on Highway 405 just east of Plaquemine.
The Ascension Parish Emergency Manager reported several trees down in the Gonzales area.
The Ascension Parish Emergency Manager reported a tree blown down onto a vehicle near the intersection of Highway 44 and Highway 941. Time of the event was estimated by radar.
The local newspaper in Houma reported a service trailer was blown over in Montegut.
The Ascension Parish Emergency Manager reported several trees were blown down in the Galvez area. Event time was estimated by radar.

A National Weather Service Storm Survey confirmed a weak EF1 tornado. The track was approximately one half mile long and 30 yards wide. Several homes had roof damage and windows blown in. One mobile home was heavily damaged. Large tree limbs were snappped and a service van was flipped over and rolled 20 feet.
WAFB-TV in Baton Rouge reported extensive street flooding in the Old Scenic Highway area. Several vehicles were submerged. The entrance to Sweet Briar Mobile Home Park was impassible.
High water was reported on many roads. A nursing home had water coming under the doorway in Greenwell Springs.
A large tree was blown down near the St. Tammany-Tangipahoa Parish near Highway 40.
Approximately 100 to 150 homes were flooded in Tangipahoa.
Many roads were reported under water in Kentwood.
The Kentwood Police Department reported 6 water rescues as a result of flooding along a creek in the village of Tangipahoa.

Louisiana State Troop L in Mandeville reported several water rescues underway with many roads impassible in the northeast quadrant of St. Helena Parish in the vicinity of Beaver Creek. Highways 441...440 and 38 were reported impassible.

A tornado touched down just south of Interstate 12 and west of Louisiana Highway 434, crossed the interstate, and then impacted Fairhope Subdivision. Windows were blown out and garage door, roof and brick veneer damage noted. Intermittent EF0 damage was observed, with very spotty EF1 damage continuing to the northeast, crossing Louisiana Highway 36, Louisiana Highway 41, and ending on the west bank of the Pearl River. Estimated wind speed was 95 to 100 mph.

A NWS Storm Survey has determined that damage in the Picayune area was a confirmed EF1 tornado with a path length of 3 miles and path width of 100 yards. This tornado was either the same tornado or formed from the same meso cyclone that produced damage earlier in St Tammany Parish before it crossed the large Pearl River Basin swamp. The track started with mostly EF0 damage on Jackson Landing Road and continued northeast across South Beech Street and Goodyear Boulevard, where the EF1 damage was noted to a residence near 6th Street and Forest, due to a large pine tree snapping and landing on the home. The tornado began dissipating and only minor damage was found near Highway 11 and Carroll Street.

A tornado touched down along Esbon Road. One wood frame house was lifted off of tied down cinder block foundation and destroyed. One other home had about half of the roofing deck from the backside of the home removed. Softwood pine trees had all limbs removed and bark missing from parts of trees. Estimated wind speed 115 mph.

A couple of power poles were blown down. Minor fence damage was reported along Joe Yenni Boulevard. A few trees were uprooted and one tree fell onto the corner of a house on Platt Street. Traffic lights were twisted on Joe Yenni Boulevard. Maximum wind was estimated at 70 mph. The tornado moved into Lake Pontchartrain.
Multiple streets reported flooded with water in 2 houses.

A tornado touched down near Pearl Drive and Azalea Lane and proceeded north-northeast for approximately 2 miles to near Davis Landing Road. Approximately 30 homes were damaged in Lake Village Subdivision. Some homes had portions of roofing deck removed. Other damage occurred near Lewis Stables...with one home sustaining a total roof loss, with a partial roof loss of another home. The tornado was rated at the lower end of the EF2 range.
Standing water was reported on Interstate 10 at Irish Bayou. Also received reports of several inches of water in the road at City Hall in Old Town Slidell.
Roof and structure damage was reported along Allen Road in west Gulfport.
A tornado touched down along Landon Road. One home had a portion of roof removed, as well as a storage building and awning destroyed. Several trees were blown down and large branches snapped.
Thunderstorm wind gusts damaged several homes in the Turnberry Subdivision. Three homes sustained roof damage, 16 homes suffered minor wind damage with siding pulled off of some homes.
Sign of Captain Ali's Restaurant blown down, as well as a power pole, along State Route 605 and Dedeaux Road.

A tornado touched down near Cedar Lake Road and Popps Ferry Road. Several mobile homes were damaged. One moblie home was rolled and destroyed with minor to moderate damage on several others. Several large tree limbs snapped as well. The tornado was rated at the upper end of EF1 scale.
Trees were reported down on Lickskillet Road north of D'Iberville.
Trees were blown down on Oaklawn Road northwest of Biloxi.
Water was overflowing the banks of the canal between West Napoleon and Severn.
Water was reported over Vista Road.
Trees were reported down on Polktown Road and also at Highway 613 in northern Jackson County.
The AWS site at Gulf Coast Community College measured a 60 mph wind gust. The report was relayed by a WLOX-13 TV meteorologist. Time of event was estimated.
Some street flooding was reported on Chapman Road and along Harrison Avenue.
Numerous large tree branches were reported down.
The tornado that occurred in Kenner at 0608CST moved north over Lake Pontchartrain as a waterspout until it was no longer visible.
Small trees were blown down. The soffit was ripped off of a bank drive through. A metal roof was pulled off of one home. Survey indicated damage was caused by straight line winds.
Additional reports of penny to quarter size hail were received from Bayou Sorrel.
Broadcast media passed on a viewer report of at least quarter size hail with some larger hailstones mixed in.

Several reports of hail were received ranging from penny and nickel size to golf ball size was reported from about 3 miles west of Laplace to the west and north portion of Laplace near the Interstate 10-Interstate 55 interchange.

The survey team found damage in the Edgard area consistent with a weak EF0 tornado and estimated winds of 65 mph. Large limbs were down, the corner of a roof lost shingles. Maximum path width of 50 yards, path length 250 yards.
A weak EF0 tornado touched down with estimated winds of 65 mph. Tree limb damage was observed and a vehicle had its camper top torn off.
Photo received from a Baton Rouge television station of slightly larger than baseball size hail, measuring 3 inches in diameter, along Highway 63 southeast of Clinton.
Photo received from Baton Rouge television station of golf ball size hail at Bluff Creek.
Emergency management received a report from the public of quarter size hail in Luling.
A trained spotter reported quarter size hail just east of New Orleans International Airport.
The Walthall County Emergency Manager reported golf ball size hail in Dinan.
Lemon to hen egg size hail was reported south of Jayess or just east of Enon near Highway 583.

A trained spotter reported water approaching homes on Roosevelt Avenue south of the West Metairie Canal and the street was not passable. Widespread street flooding was also reported in the Airline Park subdivision.
The Jefferson Parish Emergency Manager reported quarter size hail at the intersection of Manhattan Blvd and the Westbank Expressway.
A trained spotter reported half dollar size hail in Marrero.
The Cooperative Observer in Terrytown reported quarter size hail covering his yard.
Fifty power poles were snapped along Manhattan Blvd. Minor structural damage was observed on numerous buildings. The Walmart on Manhattan Blvd had major roof damage.
The COOP observer in Terrytown measured a 60 mph wind gust.
A tree was blown down onto a house on Hero Drive in Harvey.

The greatest concentration of damage was in Gretna on Manhattan Blvd, where nearly 1.8 miles of hail and wind damage occurred. Over a mile of power lines were either snapped or pushed over by these winds. An awning was blown down at the Manhattan Place Shopping Center, which damaged several cars in the parking lot.
Golf ball size hail was reported along Highway 406 and Highway 23.

Damage in Belle Chasse was in line with the storm in the Gretna area. Trees and power lines were blown down and structures received minor damage. A NWS Storm Survey showed straight line winds of 100 mph and were associated with a strong inflow notch radar signature.
A commercial building along Avenue A and Highway 23 was damaged. The front door was ripped off. Five employees toook shelter in a closet during the event.
The Plaquemines Parish Government office measured a wind gust of 100 mph at the end of Avenue G and Main Street near Plaquemines Pride.
A government building was damaged at 8056 Highway 23.
Eight inches of water was covering Highway 23 south of Belle Chasse. Moderate to heavy street flooding occurred across northern Plaquemines Parish.

Numerous streets were flooded around Harvey along Manhattan and Lapalco Boulevards. Two to three feet of water was reported on Gretna Blvd. Water was approaching, but not moving into, homes in this area.
Received a public report of quarter size hail in Chalmette.
Hail to the size of nickels and quarters occurred south of Lettsworth.
Jefferson Parish Emergency Management reported water in 25 apartments in the 1600 block of Carol Sue in Terrytown.

The survey team found tornado damage consistent with estimated winds around 105 mph. The vacant 3 story Delacroix Government Complex lost its top two floors, and suffered a collapse of north and east facing brick veneer. Five unstrapped RV trailers were flipped. Two trailers rolled for 45 yards and were totally destroyed. The tornado touched down on Bayou Terre Au Beoufs by the government complex, crossed a marsh field, and recrossed Highway 300 where 4 of the 5 trailers were affected, then lifted over the bayou. Length 0.6 miles, width 25 yards.
The public reported golf ball size hail and broken windows in the Delacroix area.
A trained spotter reported quarter size hail in the city of Amite.
A funnel cloud was reported near Delacroix.
A Baton Rouge television station relayed a public report of quarter size hail in Fordoche.

events.cz_name: COASTAL WATERS FROM SOUTHWEST PASS OF THE MISSISSIPPI RIVER TO PORT FOURCHON LOUISIANA OUT 20 NM

events.event_narrative: Power was out on Grand Isle. Transformers blew out and power lines were damaged by wind.
A tree was blown down blocking Como Road 1 mile west of Highland Road.
Trees were blown down and blocking Mahoney Road at Airport Road.
Trees were blown down and blocking Bains Road just west of Stirling Road.
A 2 foot diameter tree was blown down 1 mile southwest of New Roads.
Multiple trees were blown down along Louisiana Highway 421 between Louisiana Highway 10 and Louisiana Highway 967. The road was blocked in multiple areas.
Baton Rouge TV stations report trees and powerlines down across several locations in Baton Rouge. Over 20,000 customers were without power. Time estimated based on radar.
Trees and fences were blown down on South Foster Drive in Baton Rouge.
Baton Rouge media reported trees down on powerlines. Time estimated based on radar.
Trees were blown over and completely blocking the intersection of Coursey and Stumberg Lane.
The Pike County Emergency Manager reported trees down in McComb.

Trees, power lines and large tree branches were blown down in areas northwest to northeast of Gonzales, including areas near Walnut Road, Fairchild Road, Denham Road,  Preston Landry Road, and Hilbert Young Road.
Large tree limbs were snapped and a small tree was uprooted along Louisiana Highway 42.
Multiple trees and power lines were blocking Louisiana Highway 431 between Churchpoint/Stringer Bridge and Weber City Road.
Trees were reported down along Gold Place Road in St. Amant.
Trees were reported down blocking Stringer Ridge Road.
A large tree was snapped on Louisiana Highway 441. Time was estimated based on radar.
Several trees, power lines, tree branches were reported down along with a fence blown down. The damage occurred along Pertiuis Road, Sam Martin Road, and Highway 22.
A tree was reported down along Louisiana Highway 43 in Hungarian Settlement.
Several trees and a few power lines were downed in Amite.
Trees were reported down with the roof blown off of one shed about 2 miles east of Tylertown on Mississippi Highway 48. Time estimated based on radar.

A large portion of the roof structure was completely removed from one home. Several very large trees were completely uprooted. Two single wide mobile homes also had roof damage. Damage path length was approximately 0.2 miles. Path width of 75 yards. Winds were rated as high end EF1 with maximum wind speeds of 105 mph.
A roof was damaged and possibly blown off of a framed house near the intersection of Bogue Chitto River and Louisiana Highway 25. Time was estimated based on radar.
Trees were blown down along Interstate 12 near the Interstate 55 interchange.

A brief tornado touchdown occurred along Lower Rome Road just north of Chapel Road. The tornado roughly traveled due east along Lower Rome Road causing significant damage to trees. Several large hardwoods were uprooted and a few snapped. in addition, a metal roof was peeled off of one home. Maximum estimated winds were 100 mph. Path width was 50 yards and path length one half mile.

A tornado touchdown occurred near the intersection of North Airline Avenue and Louisiana Highway 3125. The tornado moved south-southeast through a residential neighborhood with the worst damage observed on Ezildore Avenue between 6th and 7th Streets. A carport was lifted off a home causing significant damage to the home. The tornado continued to the south-southeast causing significant tree damage and some minor to moderate roof damage. The tornado finally lifted near the end of East 2nd Street. Maximum estimated winds were 80 mph.
Trees and power lines were reported downed in Gramercy.
A few trees and power line poles were downed by thunderstorm winds in Franklinton.

A tornado lifted a trailer off the ground and blew it about 20 yards into another camper. Sheet metal and tin roofing and an awning were blown 50 to 75 yeards away and wrapped around one tree trunk about 20 feet off the ground. Numerous hardwoods and softwoods were uprooted and snapped. The tornado was witnessed by one resident. Maximum estimated winds were 105 mph.
Widespread power outages occurred in LaPlace. Trees were reported down and other debris near 2217 Airline Highway. A tree was also down across a residential handicap ramp.
A large oak tree was uprooted and fell on a house just off Louisiana Highway 41. A large portion of the house was crushed.
A branch fell through a trailer on Choctaw Road.

Several trees and large tree branches were blown down in Old Mandeville, blocking Villere Road and Monroe Street. Power was out across much of the area south of US Highway 190 and East Causeway Approach and west of Louisiana Highway 59.
A sustained wind of 40 mph with a gust to 67 mph was measured at Mid Lake Pontchartrain at the 8 mile marker.

A large tree about 3 to 4 feet in diameter was blown down and blocking US Highway 190 between Colbert and Soult Streets. Numerous power outages were reported east of Louisiana Highway 59 to Soult Street, north of US Highway 190 and south of Louisiana Highway 1088.
Large tree limbs were blown down along Interstate 59 near Mile Marker 33. Time was estimated based on radar.
Trees were reported down in the Forest Brook Subdivision off of Louisiana Highway 1088 on Mesa Court, Bluff Court, and Range Court. Time estimated based on radar.
Power lines were reported down on Airline Highway.
Trees and power lines were reported downed in Lacombe.
Power poles and trees leaning on a house with additional roof and siding damage to at least 2 other homes on Park Drive South.
Several trees and power lines down were blown down in Old Metairie, and a gas station awning was blown down.
Metal roof panels curled up on an industrial garage on Bobcat Road. Time estimated by radar.
Roof damage was reported to one home. Time was estimated based on radar.
The roof was torn off of one home on Connie Hairiel Road.
Shutters were damaged and large tree limbs downed in Luling on Kayle Drive. Time was estimated based on radar.
A tree fell on a home in Slidell near the intersection of 7th Street and Fremaux Avenue. Time of the event was based on radar.
The emergency manager reported a tree down and blocking the road in the Chamale Cove Subdivision.
A tree was reported down across US Highway 11 near St. Joe Brick Works between Slidell and Pearl River. Time was estimated based on radar.
Damage was reported to commercial buildings on Pontchartrain Drive. Two metal roofs were blown off buildings and carried down the road and numerous doors were blown in on a couple of buildings.

Multiple trees were snapped off, a few soft woods and one hard wood tree. Two hard wood trees were uprooted. Forty percent of a metal roof was blown off a house with a few roof beams broken off. The beams and metal roof were blown about 150 yards to the east. Maximum estimated winds 95 mph, maximum width about 50 yards, and a path length of 400 yards.
Two trees were reported down across Crazy Horse Drive west of Mississippi Highway 603.
A tree was blown down on Rocky Hill Dedeaux Road just east of Mississippi Highway 603.
A tree fell on a power line on South Street near Clemont Harbor.
Roof blown off of businesses in the Northwood Hills Shopping Center at 12100 Highway 49. Trees were also reported down near Orange Grove Road.
Thunderstorm winds caused roof damage to a business in Dulac.

Roofing was peeled off of a couple of metal commercial buildings in the Fountainbleau area. Windows were blown out of two houses. Large sections of two fences were blown down. Several medium trees were blown down and large tree limbs were snapped. Damage path was approximately 0.1 mile long and 75 yards wide. Estimated strength of tornado was low end EF1.
Two trees were blown down onto power lines near Cut Off.
Several trees were downed and nickel size hail was reported in the Norwood area.
Eight trees were blown down in the Thompson community.
Hail was observed on Interstate 55.
Large hail and 70 mph wind gusts were reported on Interstate 55.
Large hail and 70 mph wind gusts were reported on Interstate 55.
Large hail was observed near McComb.
A tree was blown down onto a house.
Golf ball size hail was reported by the emergency manager near Mississippi Highway 583 and East Sunny Hill Road.
Quarter size hail was reported in Plaquemine near Dow Chemical.
Quarter size hail was reported in the Riverbend Subdivision in Baton Rouge.
Quarter size hail was reported on Jones Creek Road.
Quarter size hail was reported and several trees were downed.
Quarter size hail was reported and several trees were downed.
Golf ball size hail was reported at the Mall of Louisiana, along with a rotating wall cloud.
Several trees were also reported downed.
Several trees were reported downed, along with quarter size hail.
Several trees were downed on Lawrence Creek Road. Pea size hail was reported in Pine.
The Mayor of Angie reported golf ball size hail covering his yard.
A trained spotter recorded a 59 mph wind gust. Large tree limbs were blown down, and a nearby fence was blown down.
Several large tree branches and a few trees were blown down on the west side of McComb.  One of the trees fell onto a house. A 3 year old child was fatally injured and  2 others were injured.
A tree was blown down in the community of Central.
Hail was falling heavily at times at the fire station on Louisiana Highway 37.

A waterspout was observed crossing Grand Isle. The waterspout went ashore near the bridge, crossed the island and then moved north back over the water. Grand Isle police observed the waterspout for approximately 6 miles...mainly over the water. Power lines were downed near the bridge on Louisiana Highway 1. Part of a roof was taken off of a cabin at the Bridgeside Marina.
Quarter size hail was reported at Mile Marker 16 on Interstate 59.
A tornado was reported in the Sunrise area. The Parish Sheriff's Office reported a sign was damaged in front of the South Plaquemines Parish High School in Buras along Louisiana Highway 23.
Several reports of trees down across Greenwell Springs Road were received.

A weak tornado touched down removing a portion of a house roof along with the back wall of the house. An outbuilding and shed were heavily damaged, and tin and insulation were wrapped in trees. A large tree was knocked over along with several large tree limbs snapped.
A weak tornado touched down removing a large portion of roof and exterior wall from pre-fab type house. Large trees limbs were snapped and sheet metal wrapped in trees.

events.event_narrative: A trained spotter reported quarter size hail in Diamondhead.
Golf ball size hail was reported on Mississippi Highway 63. The hail covered the roadway and grass. Hail fell from the George County line southward to the town of Wade.
Reports were received of power outages and blown transformers in Vancleave.

Damage began at Birtrue Road east of Louisiana Highway 40. The tornado then continued eastward producing EF2 damage to homes on Birtue and Thornhill Roads. EF3 damage was observed near the intersection of Jenkins Cemetery Road and Louisiana Highway 40. Two homes had extensive damage with 90 percent of their roofs ripped off and collapse of some exterior walls. Three homes suffered significant damage, as well as 10 to 15 un-anchored mobile homes.
One tree and numerous limbs were knocked down at Louisiana Highway 59 and Interstate 12. Marble size hail was also reported.
Large trees were blown down along Louisiana Highway 1088 near Cypress Street.
Hail ranging in size from marble to half dollar size was observed at the National Weather Service Office.
Quarter size hail was reported by an off duty NWS employee.
Nickel to quarter size hail was reported in the Irish Bayou area near Interstate 10.
Hail the size of quarters was reported in the Marrero-Lafitte-Larose Highway area near Lafitte.

A weak tornado touched down about 1/4 mile southwest of the intersection of Mississippi Highway 63 and Mississippi Highway 613, and travelled intermittently for approximately 3 miles to the northeast. A portable office building was flipped over, power lines were blown down, and several trees were knocked down.
A gas station awning was heavily damaged and several power poles were blown down along Airline Highway. A nearby refinery recorded wind gusts of 70 mph before power failed.
Several trees were blown down near Holmesville.
Hail one half to one inch in diameter was reported in southern Denham Springs near Range Avenue and Vincent Road.
A carport was torn off a home in the Shenandoah area of Baton Rouge, and wind caused roof damage to a supermarket on George O'Neal Road.  Time of the event was estimated by radar.

Shingles, siding and roofing material was blown from car dealerships and other businesses across the intersection of Sherwood Forest and Airline Highway. Trees were also reported down on Cedarcrest Avenue.
Power outages were reported at the Mall of Louisiana. Event time was estimated based on radar.
Roof damage was reported to a home on Louisiana Highway 42 on the north side of Prairieville. Event time was estimated based on radar.

Downburst wind damage occurred in the Brusley and Addis areas. An apartment building had portion of its roof blown off and some brick veneer peeled off. A commercial building was also damage. Several trees were snapped along with power poles.
A few reports of hail up to quarter size were received from the New Roads area.
Several trees were blown down and blocking roads in Zachary. Trees were also reported down on at least 3 homes.
Trees were reported down in the Ventress area southeast of New Roads.
Trees were reported downed in the New Roads area.
Quarter size hail was reported in Hurley.
A few trees were reported blown down in Tylertown.
Quarter size hail was observed in Ponchatoula.
Damage was observed to a sign and other minor property damage at a gas station on Brownswitch Road near U.S. Highway 11.
Golf ball size hail was reported at the rest area on Interstate 10 just west of the Louisiana-Mississippi state line.
Quarter size hail was observed at the National Weather Service office.
Broadcast media relayed a report of half dollar size hail at the intersection of Hollywood Street and Plank Road in North Baton Rouge.
Louisiana State Police reported quarter size hail in Denham Springs.
Ice cube size hail was reported at U.S. Highway 49 and School Road north of Gulfport.
Quarter size hail was reported 1 mile northwest of Lyman.
Quarter size hail was reported at Mississippi Highway 53 and Shaw Road in Lyman.
Quarter size hail was reported in Port Allen.
Quarter size hail was reported at the intersection of Bouie Road and Robert Dossett Road in southeast Pearl River County.
Half dollar size hail was reported at Anchor Lake Road and Bouie Road.
A few trees were blown down in the city of McComb.
Quarter size hail was reported just north of Franklinton.
Nickel to quarter size hail was reported near the Industrial Canal and Mississippi River Gulf Outlet area.
Quarter size hail was reported 4 miles southeast of Denham Springs.
Lightning struck a house on Garden Lake Court in Baton Rouge, which started a fire in the attic. Two residents were home, but no injuries were reported.

COASTAL WATERS FROM BOOTHVILLE LOUISIANA TO SOUTHWEST PASS OF THE MISSISSIPPI RIVER OUT 20 NM

events.event_narrative: Power lines were downed and nickel size hail reported. Event time was estimated based on radar.
A house on Charleston Road was struck by lightning.
A 90 foot communications tower collapsed about 15 feet above its base at the Ascension Parish Department of Public Works Building. Report received by web posting and confirmed by NWS.
A number of trees were blown down by, and a vehicle with a trailer was overturned due to high winds on Interstate 59 near Gumpond-Beal Road 3 miles north of Hillsdale Exit 35.
A lightning strike started a fire at a camp in Oscar.
Several large trees were knocked down blocking Louisiana Highway 78 near Louisiana Highway 1 near Oscar.
An oak tree and a small pine tree were blown down by a microburst on the west side of Harrison County just north of Interstate 10.
Trees were down across the road near the intersection of Louisiana Highway 1 and Louisiana Highway 972. Parish maintenance was dispatched to clear the trees from the road.
Several trees were reported down on Singley Road west of Angie. A power outage was reported in Angie.
A large tree branch fell on a vehicle near City Park in Baton Rouge.
A funnel cloud was briefly observed by the weather observer at New Orleans International Airport. The funnel cloud was observed in the Destrehan area of St. Charles Parish.
Several trees were knocked down along U.S. Highway 11 in McNeil.
Trees were blown down near the intersection of U.S. Highway 61 and Louisiana Highway 54. One tree fell on a business.
One tree was blown down and a trampoline was overturned in a yard, along with pea size hail, along Walker South Road to the south of the town of Walker.
The Livingston Parish Emergency Manager reported tree damage, power lines down, and some damage to an apartment complex along Eden Church Road near U.S. Highway 190 between Walker and Denham Springs.
Livingston Parish Sheriff's Department reported trees down along Gaylord Road in the southern portion of Walker.
Terrebonne Parish Emergency Manager reported downed trees, downed power lines and an overturned trailer home in the Bobtown Community along Grand Calliou Road.

The St. Tammany Parish Emergency Manager reported power lines down, tree branches down, and some roofing material off of outbuildings along Jack Fork Road outside of Folsom. Straight line winds estimated at 60 mph.
Broadcast media reported a tree downed and blocking the road at Beechwood Drive and Byron Avenue. A wind gust of 52 mph was recorded at the Baton Rouge Airport on the north side of Baton Rouge.
The observer at New Orleans Lakefront Airport observed a waterspout over Lake Pontchartrain. Public reports of up to 5 different waterspouts were received around the same time.

events.event_narrative: A waterspout was observed that later moved onshore Grand Isle as a waterspout then moved into Barataria Bay. See other severe weather event entry for damage at Grand Isle.

Jefferson Parish officials confirmed through local newspaper that 4 homes were flooded on Holmes Boulevard in Terrytown. Widespread flooding of streets occurred in west bank areas of Jefferson Parish including Terry Parkway, Carrolton Parkway, several other roadways.
The St. Bernard Parish President reported widespread flooding across the parish with many streets impassible due to deep water.
Harrison County Dispatch reported U.S. Highway 90 in southwestern Harrison County was closed due to high water flowing over the road as a result of heavy rainfall.
Widespread and deep street flooding was reported in Houma.
Three homes experienced flooding in Raceland. Widespread street flooding was also reported in Thibodaux, but no homes were flooded.
A few roads were reported closed in the Lacombe area due to flooding.

Several reports of street flooding were received from the Metairie area, including parts of Airline Highway, Jefferson Highway, and some smaller residential streets. Jefferson Highway was nearly impassible at Clearview.
Police reported street flooding of Loyola Drive and West Esplanade. Hooper Drive at Loyola Drive was also reported flooded.
Broadcast media reported that a person was struck and killed by lightning while on the pier at Pascagoula Beach Pier.

events.cz_name: COASTAL WATERS FROM BOOTHVILLE LOUISIANA TO SOUTHWEST PASS OF THE MISSISSIPPI RIVER OUT 20 NM

events.event_narrative: The Lake Pontchartrain Causeway Police reported a waterspout just west of the bridge near Mile Marker 20.
A man working on a roof in Houma was overcome by heat and died. Heat index values were near 105 degrees at the time.

Lightning struck near a large group of people gathered for a four-wheel vehicle event north of Covington. Firefighters evaluated at least a dozen people who had minor injuries, and three people were taken to the hospital.
Quarter size hail covered the ground.
Thunderstorm wind gusts downed a tree near the intersection of Mississippi Highway 583 and Mississippi Highway 336.
Extensive power outages were reported in Zachary. Tree limbs and power lines were reported downed, with roof damage to one home.
Trees were reported down along Island Road and Oakland Road. Entergy Power indicated spotty power outages along Island Road, generally south of New Roads and Lower False River Road.
Trees were reported down one mile west of Pearl River.
Large tree limbs and powerlines were reported downed by thunderstorm winds.
Thunderstorm wind gusts downed a couple of dead trees and a number of large tree limbs near several roads north and northeast of Kiln.
Funnel cloud encoded in observation 6 miles southwest of KBIX. Law enforcement also reported waterspout in this area.
Waterspout reported moving onshore by law enforcement near Courthouse Road. Dissipation occurred at 1255 CDT. No damage reported.
Lightning sparked a fire that caused an estimated $1 milliion in damage to the Gator Stop Super Truck Stop and Casino.
Golfball size hail was reported south of Denham Springs.
Quarter size hail was reported in Walker.
A tree was blown down across U.S. Highway 190 between Juban Road and Eden Church Road.
A tree was blown down on a house on Dabney Drive.
A tree was blown down on a house on Burgess Avenue.
Several streets were flooded in Waggaman and Harvey areas of Jefferson Parish due to heavy rain. Around 2.6 inches of rain fell in one hour.

events.cz_name: COASTAL WATERS FROM SOUTHWEST PASS OF THE MISSISSIPPI RIVER TO PORT FOURCHON LOUISIANA OUT 20 NM
events.event_narrative: A large waterspout was spotted by sheriffs offices and the public near the Fort Jackson area, over Yellow Cotton Bay, close to the Mississippi River.
Many secondary roadways were flooded inlcuding portions of Louisiana Highway 22. A combination of high tides and heavy rainfall caused 250 houses to be affected by primarily minor flooding.
Approximately 100 homes had minor flooding in in the Laffitte and Crown Point area. In the Grand Isle areas flooding of low lying property occurred on the bay sides.
Low land flooding occurred in many areas. Louisiana Highway 1 was flooded south of Golden Meadow, and flooding affected Louisiana Highway 24.

Flooding affected low lying areas outside the hurricane protection levee. Approximately 6 miles of parish maintained back levees were overtopped or breached in the areas Myrtle Grove and West Point a la Hache causing flooding along Louisiana Highway 23.
Flooding affected low lying areas outside the hurricane protection levee.
Flooding affected low lying areas and roadways outside the hurricane protection levee.
Flooding affected low lying areas and roadways outside the hurricane protection levee in far east New Orleans near Fort Pike and Venetian Isles.
Quarter size hail fell at Rayburn Correctional institute along Louisiana Highway 21 north of Varnado. Nickel size hail was still falling at the time of the report.
In the town of Greenwell Springs, quarter size hail was reported and hail was beginning to accumulate on the grass.
A few hail stones as large as 2 inches in diameter, as well as numerous golf ball size hailstones were observed in Greenwell Springs. Hail size estimated from video.
Wind driven golf ball size hail broke car windows in Hammond.
The AWOS at Hammond Airport reported a wind gust of 67 mph.
Golf ball size hail was reported south of Denham Springs.
Quarter size hail was observed in Walker.
A tree was blown down across U. S. Highway 190 between Jubin Road and Eden Church Road.
A tree was blown down on a home on Dabney Drive.
A tree was blown down on a home on Burgess Avenue.
Three waterspouts were reported at the same time south of Gulfport Harbor.
Flooding occurred in low lying areas and roadways south of Ponchatoula.
Flooding occurred in low lying areas on both east and west bank areas outside of the hurricane protection levees.
Storm surge flooding affected low lying areas and roadways around Frenier.

Storm surge flooding along Lake Pontchartrain resulted in flooding of low lying roadway and property. Approximately 60 houses had minor flooding in the Slidell, Lacombe, Mandeville and Madisonville areas.
Minor flooding occurred outside of the hurricane protection levees.
Minor flooding occurred outside of the hurricane protection levees.
Minor flooding occurred outside of the hurricane protection levees.
Minor storm surge flooding impacted low lying roadways near the coast and bays, especially at times of high astronomical tides.
Minor storm surge flooding impacted low lying roadways near the coast and bays, especially at times of high astronomical tides.
Minor storm surge flooding impacted low lying roadways near the coast and bays, especially at times of high astronomical tides.

Flash Flooding was reported in Walker and other areas of Livingston Parish due to heavy rain associated with Tropical Storm Lee. Roadway flooding occurred as well as minor flooding to houses.  High tide levels restricted runoff resulting in additional flood issues.
Heavy rainfall from Tropical Storm Lee resulted in flooding causing minor flooding to five houses.
Heavy rainfall from Tropical Storm Lee resulted in flooding in several areas of Jackson County.  Eleven houses had minor flooding in Moss Point.

A tornado touchdown occurred near the intersection of Pilate Lane and Bayou Road. The tornado touched down near the flood wall and moved NNE across Pilate Lane. It caused significant damage to one trailer, separating the roof from the walls. It also snapped several large tree branches, downed a wooden fence, and destroyed a wooden shed. Near Bayou Road, the tornado caused minor damage to a brick home and snapped an 18 inch diameter tree near the base. From there, the tornado continued NNE into a marshy area where damage was observed in the tree tops. Total surveyed path was roughly 0.5 miles, but the path may have been longer through the marshy area into Lake Borgne. Maximum sustained winds were estimated at 100 mph. Path width 50 yards.

A weak tornado moving southeast to northwest touched down for a short distance. A mobile home was turned on its side, the tops of trees were snapped, and a few small trees snapped. Estimated strength was upper end EF0. Path length was 0.1 mile and the path width 30 yards.

A weak tornado moved along an intermittent path for approximately 0.6 miles. Large tree limbs were snapped and several trees were blown down. Shingles were peeled from a garage and aluminum fascia was peeled off of an eave. The tornado also tossed a single engine Cessna aircraft that had been chained to anchors about 35 yards, severely damaging it. Additionally, a pontoon boat that had been anchored to shore, was ripped from its mooring anchors and badly damaged. Path width was approximately 100 yards. Maximum rating was low end EF1.

A weak tornado moved along an intermittent path for about 3.6 miles. Large tree limbs were snapped, several trees were blown down and fences blown down. Roof damage to several homes occurred, as well as mobile home damage. Damage path was 3.6 miles, path width 75 yards. Maximum rating low end EF1.
Several trees were reported blown down just west of Liberty.

The tornado began about 5 miles northeast of Greensburg. Track length was approximately one half mile long with a path width of 150 yards. Estimated maximum winds were around 105 mph. Damage was reported to one residence, which was blown about 10 feet off its foundation. The home also had a collapse of one exterior wall. Scattered trees and power lines were also blown down.

Damage was confined to Lafayette Woods Boulevard and Piping Rock Drive. Large areas of shingles were removed off one home. An awning was thrown over a home. One boat was flipped. Multiple tree tops were snapped. A shed was blown out of a residential yard with debris sent into the Village East Elementary School grounds. Some debris was lifted 50 feet up into the trees. Three windows were blown out at the school. Track length was 100 yards and width was 25 yards. Damage rated at EF0.
Damage was reported in the Kingspoint Subdivision southeast of Slidell. Trees were snapped with one tree damaging the roof of a home. Several fences were also blown down.

Naturally occurring higher terrain along the east bank of the Mississippi River protected communities from the Mississippi flood waters.  However, considerable flooding of low land areas occurred near the Mississippi River. Some temporary structures such as fishing-hunting camps were flooded.  Several houses and local businesses were were flooded or isolated due to flooded roadways and property.

Considerable low land flooding occurred in the extreme west portion of the county near the Mississippi River. County emergency management reported approximately 50 houses and 80 mobile homes were affected by floodwaters. Several roads and bridges in the west portion of the parish were damaged by flooding.
Several power lines were reported down in Clinton.
Trees and power lines were reported down on Louisiana Highway 444 east of King George Bay Road and Louisiana Highway 22, 5 miles southeast of French Settlement.
A large oak tree was reported down on Black Cat Road.
Trees were reported blown down at Kirklin Road and U.S. Highway 98.
An awning was blown down onto a car in a residential area of St. Rose.
Trees and power lines were downed on Highway 956 near the intersection of Highway 10 and Highway 19 south of Wilson.
Trees and power lines were reported downed on Highway 19 in Norwood. The highway was closed for a period of time.
Power lines were reported down in the Bonnabel and West End areas.

A weak tornado touched down near Holly Drive just west of Slaughter and tracked northeast on an intermittent path to just north of the intersection of Louisiana Highway 956 and Louisiana Highway 412. Several houses had roofing shingles and soffit removed. Several large trees were snapped, large tree limbs snapped, and trees down on power lines. Most damage was EF0, with a few areas of low end EF1 damage. Path length was approximately 3 miles and path width 30 yards.

A multiple vehicle accident with several fatalities, numerous injuries and a large societal impact occurred in the pre-dawn hours along a stretch of Interstate Highway 10 in a marshy area in New Orleans East around 430 am CST. Patchy radiational fog was developing, with smoke from a local ongoing peat sub-surface fire a potentially additional contributing factor to restricting visibility. Forty vehicles, including numerous freight tractor-trailers, and early morning commuters, were involved on both the east and westbound lanes of Interstate 10. The interstate was closed for approximately 12 hours after the accident.

A weak tornado touched down and ripped siding and a portion of the roof off a metal boat storage building, snapped a couple of small trees, destroyed a storage shed at a residence, and moved a shipping container 30 feet. Maximum wind speed was estimated at 80 mph, path width was 30 yards, path length was 400 yards.

A tornado touched down just off of Ott Stanford Road. A patio roof was peeled back and ripped off half of the roof of one home. The tornado traveled to the northeast and destroyed a small well shed and then tore another patio roof off of a second home. The tornado continued to the northeast, finally snapping one small pine tree before lifting. Maximum wind speed was estimated at 75 mph, path width was 100 yards, path length was 200 yards.
Several pine trees were blown down.
A tree and several power lines were blown down in Grosse Tete.
A tree was blown down in the St. Gabriel area.
Nickel to quarter size hail was observed by West Baton Rouge Sheriffs deputies in Port Allen.
Several trees were blown down in Ponchatoula. Event time was estimated based on radar.
Several trees were blown down in Robert. Event time was estimated based on radar.
Livingston Parish Sheriffs office reported several trees were blown down in the southwest portion of the parish in the vicinity of Highway 16 and Highway 1033.
Several trees were blown down onto cars in the vicinity of Green Street north of Abita Springs.
Several trees and power lines were blown down in the vicinity of Highway 43 and Pine Grove Road.

A NWS survey was conducted in Abita Springs. Damage is mainly confined to trees and power lines blown down, all in one direction. Damage is widespread and lacks a clear path. Survey results show thunderstorm straight line wind damage.
St. Tammany Sheriffs office reported several trees were blown down in the northeast portion of the parish from north of Covington to near Bush.
Trees were blown down and barns damaged near Necaise Crossing.
Several roads were closed due to high water in downtown Slidell.
Power lines were blown down at Hugh Lee Road and Road 228.
Roof blown off an abandoned trailer on Earl C. Ladner Road.
A tree was reported blown down across the road on Crane Creek Road.
Trees were reported down on Anner Road.
A back porch roof was blown off a home and was sitting on the front of a home next door on Preacher Powell Road.

Several tree limbs were blown down and 1 pine tree was snapped off about 15 to 20 feet above ground at Westgate Parkway and Farmington Drive. One home had several pieces of vinyl siding blown off one side. At a nearby RV park, there was an older motorhome RV blown on its side with an uninjured person inside.

Trees were reported down south of McNeil. Also, trees were blown down onto sheds on Clay Road near Liberty Road. Power outage affected 5,700 customers in Pearl River County. Unconfirmed public reports of a tornado in the area.
Winds blew a shed about 50 feet from its foundation and downed a few power lines in the Grand Point area. The event time was estimated from radar.
One shed was heavily damaged by thunderstorm winds in the Bayou Gauche area.

A NWS storm survey team confirmed a tornado touched down and tracked through portions of Prairieville. The tornado initially touched down along Duplessis Road, tracked approximately 3 miles before lifting after crossing near the intersection of Highways 42 and 930. Several homes received significant roof damage and many trees were uprooted or snapped. The path width was approximately 50 yards with an estimated wind speed of 110 mph.
Scattered trees were reported down across the parish.
A roof was damaged on a house on Satsuma Road east of Walker.
Pike County Emergency Management reports straight line wind damage in Magnolia with power lines down, roof damage to several barns, and trees blown down.

A weak tornado touched down just south of Varnado Road and tracked north-northwest across North Corbin Road. A home lost a portion of the roof and several trees were snapped along the track. The tornado lifted to the southwest of North Corbin Elementary School. The storm path length was approximately 0.5 miles, the path width 50 yards, and maximum strength EF1 with estimated winds of 100 mph.
A large tree was blown down which heavily damaged the roof of a home.
A tree was blown down at a wrecker service with a fence damaged. Large tree limbs were also blown down in the area.

A NWS storm survey team observed damage produced by a tornado northeast of Madisonville. The tornado touched down near the clubhouse in the Tchefuncta Country Club Estates neighborhood. The tornado continued on a path to the northeast, downing several trees and producing minor roof damage to two homes before lifting in a heavily wooded area beyond the neighborhood. The tornado had a path width of approximately 100 yards and a path length of one half mile.

Weak EF0 tornado touched down near the intersection of Silver Springs Drive and Allen Road. It moved north, snapping several pine trees. Some roof damage was observed to one home where part of a tree had fallen through the roof. The tornado lifted after crossing Jarrell Road. Maximum estimated wind speed was 65 mph, maximum width 25 yards, and path length approximately 1.5 miles. Event time was based on radar.
Trees were reported down along Callington Road.
Trees were reported down in Pearlington.
Trees were reported down near Highway 53, Lizana School Road and Saucier Lizana Road.
Flash flooding of Bonfouca Drive in the Palm Lake Subdivision was reported by the Slidell Fire Department.
Widespread street flooding reported in Diamondhead. Some severe street flooding occurred with an estimated two and a half feet depth at its deepest points.

A NWS storm survey concluded that an EF0 tornado with a path width 50 yards wide was on the ground for about one quarter mile. Winds were estimated at 70 mph. Damage was confined to a trailer at Vidalia and Walnut Roads.
Power poles were downed northwest of Pass Christian.
Numerous trees and power lines were reported downed along Beatline Road.
Severe street flooding was reported along and near U.S. Highway 90.
Numerous fires reported, including an apartment complex, at least one home, and several power poles.
Louisiana GOHSEP relayed reports of minor damage to 8 mobile homes, trees down on Louisiana Highway 996 and power poles down on Louisiana Highway 70.
Pearl River County Sheriffs Office reported high water near the intersection of Moeller and Apache Roads.

NWS Storm survey confirmed a tornado touched down on John Lee Road and Roberts Road. Trees were twisted, a travel trailer was flipped, and several homes lost portions of their roofs. The path width was 100 yards, and was on the ground for nearly 1 mile. Estimated wind speed was 90 mph.

Major street flooding on Highway 90 near Pass Christian. Major street flooding also reported north-northwest of Long Beach along 28th Street from Beatline Road to Klondyke Road, and south of Lyman on Canal Road south of Robinson Road.
Damage reported at the Hampton Inn. Possible tornado.

NWS storm survey confirmed a tornado touched down along Highway 67 at Highway 15. Most of the damage was at the starting point with a large shed door blown in, causing roof damage and a patio roof lifted off. Most of the remainder of the damage was to shingles and fences, with an end point in Coventry Estates. The path width was 100 yards with a damage track around 4 miles long. Estimated wind speed was 85 mph.
Extensive flooding beginning to be reported throughout St. Charles Parish.
Major street flooding reported in the northern part of Terrebonne Parish. Several roads were inundated and closed. No water was reported in homes. Bayou Terrebonne remained in banks.
Ten to twenty homes in the Raceland and Lockport areas had water enter them. A business in the Lockport area had approximately 4 inches of water inside. Extensive street flooding was also reported.
A waterspout was reported by Biloxi Police Department over Mississippi Sound.
Air traffic control reported a waterspout 5 miles southeast of Gulfport Airport.
Quarter size hail was reported in the vicinity of Tiger Bend Road and Antioch Road. Wind gusts of 40 to 50 mph were also reported.
Quarter size hail was reported in Zachary.
Three trees were reported blown down between Liberty and Gloster.
Quarter size hail was reported near Roosevelt Boulevard and West Metairie Avenue.
Quarter size hail was reported near Sam's Club in Kenner.
Quarter size hail fell at the National Weather Service office.
A storm spotter reported dime to quarter size hail occurring in Metairie between Causeway Boulevard and Bonnabel Boulevard.
The roof was blown off of a house at Gentilly Boulevard and Franklin Avenue. Several other homes were also damaged.
Two to three feet of standing water was reported in sections of Gentilly. Cars were stalled out in the flood water.
Nickel to quarter size hail fell for about 10 minutes in Kiln around 1 am.
Lake Pontchartrain Causeway Police reported 60 mph measured wind gust at the drawbridge.
Lightning struck a house near Morris Place and Carol Drive in Old Jefferson, causing a fire.
Public reports water entering at least one building near Mark Lane and Citrus Drive in River Ridge.

Widespread street flooding was reported with several roads impassible and several stalled cars. Standing water was reported on Interstate 10 in some locations, and at least one on ramp was closed due to standing water.
Quarter size hail was reported on Camp Wilkes Road.
Frequent wind gusts of 35 to 39 knots measured at Shell Beach between 654 am CDT and 818 am CDT.
West Feliciana Sheriffs office reported quarter size hail on Highway 61 just north of St. Francisville.
Quarter to half dollar size hail fell between the communities of Boeuf and Gibson, covering the ground in some locations.

Tangipahoa Parish Sheriffs Office reported the fatality of two fishermen due to a lightning strike along the Natalbany River. The two men had taken shelter from thunderstorms in a small metal tin structure. The nearby trees showed evidence of being struck by lightning.
Quarter size hail fell along Highway 445 north of Robert. Time was estimated based on radar.
A 39 mph gust was reported at the gage at mid Lake Pontchartrain Causeway (MDLL1).
Water was reported in 5 homes in the Mimosa Park area south of Luling. Widespread street flooding was reported across much of St. Charles Parish.
The measured gust was at GPOM6 on the west side of Ship Island.
Measured gust occurred at GPOM6 on the west side of Ship Island.
Extensive and deep street flooding was reported in Amite. Water was reported up to two feet deep on some roads.

Local television station web page traffic camera showed an underpass flooded at Acadian Throughway with a vehicle stalled in the water. Minor street flooding was also reported in the 4100 block of Essen Lane.
Heavy rain overwhelmed local drainage resulting in minor flooding of 13 homes according to reports received from Baton Rouge media and the Ascension Parish Sheriffs Office.
A house fire was started by a lightning strike in Central Baton Rouge. Damage was estimated at $70,000. No injuries were reported.
A local television station reported a house fire sparked by lightning on Hoo Shoo Too Road. One firefighter was injured while fighting the blaze. Event time was estimated.
Multiple trees were reported blown down near Mayfield Elementary School on U.S. Highway 190.
Several trees were reported blown down on Louisiana Highway 955.
Quarter size hail was reported by the public 4 miles north of Pride.
Jackson County Emergency Management reported two waterspouts just offshore. Media photos were taken of these waterspouts. Movement was to the southeast at 15 knots.

events.event_narrative: A NOAA employee observed and reported a waterspout on the north side of Grand Isle, moving slowly south. In addition, several photos and videos of the waterspout were taken by the general public. The waterspout eventually moved onshore the west portion of Grand Isle as a tornado.

A waterspout over Barataria Bay, as described in an earlier entry, moved southward and onshore the west portion of Grand Isle. A National Weather Service storm survey determined EF-1 damage. There was a total loss of one manufactured home roof, and roof and siding damage to several other structures. A parked recreational travel trailer also suffered significant damage. Some roof debris was thrown 30 yards to the northeast. The path extended from just east of Raspberry Lane on the north side of the island to just west of Raspberry street on the south side of the island. The damage ended around Louisiana Highway 1.
Several trees were blown down and several homes suffered roof damage on Hoo Shoo Too Road.
Dime to half dollar size hail fell along State Highway 24 north of Fort Adams.

A NWS storm survey confirmed a short and narrow damage path about 0.25 miles long and 100 feet wide. Eyewitnesses reported seeing a funnel cloud before residences were damaged. The damage path started near the corner of Puma and Chinchilla Streets. The damage path extended northeast to near the corner of Bear Street and Cougar Drive. Approximately 10 homes received minor damage. The most extensive damage was one carport being destroyed and also causing shingle and roof cap damage. Winds were estimated at 70 mph.
A few trees were reported uprooted in St. Francisville. A funnel cloud was briefly sighted by sheriff's deputies. Rainfall at the EOC totalled 1.75 inches.
Power lines were reported blown down near Baton Rouge Ryan Airport.
Five to ten power poles were snapped in front of a chemical plant. A trailer was also moved off its foundation in the plant area.
Quarter size hail was reported by a storm chaser southeast of Clinton.
A cooperative observer reported quarter size hail in Hammond.
Tylertown Fire Department reported golf ball size hail.
A 37 knot wind gust was measured at Lakefront Airport.
Seven power lines were blown down on State Highway 1 near the Valentine Bridge. Several trees were also reported blown down.
Several trees were reported blown down along State Highway 436 near Pine.
A 34 knot wind gust was measured at the Shell Beach C-MAN station.
A 41 knot gust was measured at the Gulfport Outer Range C-MAN station.

Heavy rain produced standing water, making roads impassible. Some locations included were the 2000 block of Woodmere Street, Armagh Street, the 1700 block of Destrehan Avenue, and the 1600 block of Long Bridge.
National Weather Service employees observed several streets across Mandeville with 1 to 2 feet of water covering the roadways, making them impassable.
A National Weather Service employee reported multiple roads on the north side of Covington had 1 to 2 feet of water covering the roadway, making them impassable.
Local law enforcement in the town of Nicholson reported a flooded and barricaded intersection at Oliver Davis Road and Section Line Road.
A 42 knot wind gust was measured at the Bay Waveland Yacht Club C-MAN station.
A 38 knot gust was measured by the Keesler AFB ASOS on the Biloxi Back Bay.
A 48 knot gust was measured at the Gulfport West Pier C-MAN station.
A 39 knot gust was measured at PTBM6.
A 36 knot wind gust was measured at Shell Beach C-MAN station.
A wind gust of 39 knots was measured at New Canal Station.
A 41 knot wind gust was measured at Lakefront Airport.
NAS New Orleans measured a wind gust of 54 knots from 200 degrees.
NAS New Orleans reported a second wind gust of 54 knots from 180 degrees at 26 after the hour.
A local newspaper reported downed trees and power lines in Marrero and Harvey due to thunderstorm winds.
Power lines were reported downed in Terrytown. Event time based on radar.
A 39 knot wind gust was measured at PTBM6.
Baton Rouge television station reported that lightning struck a tree and traveled into a nearby home starting a fire. The fire caused significant damage to one room and the roof of the home.
A large oak tree was downed across the road at Highway 57 and Jim Ramsey Road. Numerous limbs and tree debris was also reported in Vancleave.
Trees and power lines were reported down along Highway 53 between Saucier-Lizana Road and Shaw Road. Event time was estimated based on radar.
Scattered tree damage was reported in the Gentilly area. Approximately 5000 customers were reported without power in Orleans Parish.

Thunderstorm winds damaged trees at Old Spanish Trail and Terrace Avenue. Trees were reported down and debris in the road in several locations across the city of Slidell as reported by the Slidell Fire Department.
Quarter size hail was reported at Duncan Street in Slidell.
Trees were reported blown down onto cars in Kenner.
Lakefront Airport measured a wind gust of 36 knots.
Multiple waterspouts were reported and photographed just west of the Lake Pontchartrain Causeway near the north end of the bridge.
A couple of trees were reported blown down at Stennis Space Center.
A tree was reported down off of Robert Boulevard.
A waterspout moved onshore at Port Fourchon. One person was slightly injured when a security guard shack was damaged. Two autos also received damage.
Measured gust of 44 mph recorded at GWPM6.
Measured gust of 62 mph at GWPM6.
Measured gust of 51 mph at WYCM6.

A National Weather Service storm survey indicated that straight line thunderstorms toppled a weakened tree, snapped several large and small tree limbs, and caused damage to an outbuilding. The damage was noted along Cuevas Delisle Road.
A waterspout was sighted about 2 miles south of Ocean Springs, moving away from shore.

events.cz_name: COASTAL WATERS FROM SOUTHWEST PASS OF THE MISSISSIPPI RIVER TO PORT FOURCHON LOUISIANA OUT 20 NM
events.event_narrative: The Port Fourchon Harbor Police relayed a report of a waterspout southeast of Port Fourchon. Images submitted showed a narrow waterspout visible from shore.

National Weather Service employees reported deep water over several main roads in Slidell. Some locations included Airport Road near the Interstate 12 interchange, Rue Rochelle and Gause Boulevard areas.

Portions of Highway 59 and Sharp Road were under water. Half of Highway 190 near Soult was blocked off. The CVS parking lot near the intersection of Highway 1088 and Highway 59 was completely flooded.

Social media and other reports reported indicated significant and deep street flooding through portion of business district of New Orleans, including Tulane Avenue.  Some water entered the ground floor of Tulane Hospital. Washington Avenue and 4th Street, as well as St. Anthony Street were inundated. The Loyola Avenue onramp to the Pontchartrain Expressway was underwater. Areas of around South Jefferson Davis Parkway also had significant and deep street flooding.

Significant street flooding was reported in Houma. The local newspaper reported that one resident on Stovall Street had 4 feet of water in her home. The local cooperative observer reported over 6 inches of rain in Houma.
Numerous streets were impassible due to flash flooding in River Ridge, Harahan and Metairie.
Numerous streets were impassible due to flash flooding in New Orleans.
Lakefront Airport reported a peak gust of 48 mph from the northeast.
New Canal Station reported a peak gust of 45 mph from the northeast.
An off duty Air Force officer from Keesler AFB reported several trees down along Lorraine Road near Highway 67. Small hail and flooding rainfall was also reported.
A wind gust of 43 knots was measured at Lakefront Airport.
Wind damage was reported to a barn and surrounding structures between Highway 43 and Highway 11 near McNeil. The radar signature was indicative of a downburst between 1119 and 1124 CDT.
Damage was reported to fencing and small objects in the 5400 block of Tusa Drive. Pictures were posted on social media. Time of the event was estimated based on a radar fix.
Several streets were reported flooded throughout the metropolitan area. Rain rates of 2 inches per hour were reported during the peak rainfall between 130 pm and 230 pm CDT.
Trees and power lines were knocked down. Time of the event was based on radar.

Damage reported at St. Francis Animal Sanctuary. An outbuilding that houses dogs was destroyed with numerous dogs injured...one fatally. A large tree was uprooted. Numerous 600 pound dog houses were blown 50 to 120 feet. A facility on piers with straps was moved 6 feet off of the piers. Estimated wind speed was 85 mph. Path length one third of a mile and path width 500 feet.
Reports were received of 6 trees blown down in the Bayou Gauche area.
Entergy reported two power outages in the Madisonville area affecting 41 customers.
Multiple streets were impassible in Slidell, mainly across northern portions of the city. Over 5 inches of rain was measured at Slidell Airport in 2 hours and 15 minutes.
Surface observation from Keesler AFB reported a waterspout lasting from 937 am to 950 am CDT. The waterspout was also reported by broadcast media and law enforcement.
The buoy at Shell Beach reported a wind gust of 35 knots.

The St. Bernard Sheriffs Department received several calls of water near homes in Arabi. Several streets were deeply flooded and impassable including portions of Judge Perez Drive, Norton Street and Doerr Drive.

Media reported several trees blown down just east of Denham Springs.

events.event_narrative: A 53 mph gust was recorded at GISL1.

The tornado moved inland and uprooted a tree after crossing Beach Boulevard. It caused significant damage to a home under construction on the corner of 15th Street and 18th Avenue. All walls of the home were shifted and leaning, with a portion of the roof collapsed. The tornado also collapsed the porch roof of a home on 19th Avenue. It caused mainly tree damage as it continued to move NNW before lifting.

A tornado touched down in the south portion of Pascagoula. Most of the damage was consistent with EF-1 scale damage consisting of downed trees and light structural damage to a few houses. A small area of significant damage...EF-2...occurred where nearly all of the roof of a large house was blown off. Path length 0.7 miles. Path width 40 yards.

A tornado touched down in the Gulf Park Estates area causing damage to roofs on several houses and blowing out windows. A few trees were downed and large tree branches snapped. Path length approximately 0.4 miles. Path width 40 yards.

Rainbands associated with Tropical Storm Isaac persisted over Harrison County producing torrential rainfall. US Highway 49 near Orange Grove was impassable for periods of time due to flooding and several secondary roadways were flooded in the county. A number of houses also had flooding. High tide levels limited the runoff of heavy rainfall in the coastal area.

Rainbands associated with Tropical Storm Isaac persisted over Jackson County during the overnight and morning hours producing torrential rainfall. Flooding of secondary routes was reported over much of the area. A number of high water rescues were necessary when neighborhoods in the Pascagoula and Escatawpa areas were flooded in the early to mid morning.

Rainbands associated with Tropical Storm Isaac produced torrential rainfall across the county. Extensive secondary roadway flooding was reported and some houses flooded. A number of water rescues were conducted due to the flooding.  Interstate Highway 59 at mile marker 31 was closed for several hours due to flooding.
Rainbands from tropical storm Isaac persisted over the region producing heavy rainfall. Secondary roadways were flooded along with a few houses.
Rainbands from tropical storm Isaac persisted over the region producing heavy rainfall. Secondary roadways were flooded along with a few houses.
Heavy rain associated with Hurricane Isaac produced deep street flooding in the New Orleans area.

events.event_narrative: The Lake Pontchartrain Causeway Commission reported about $3 million worth of damage to the bridge across Lake Pontchartrain and supporting infrastructure. Tropical storm force winds were reported for approximately 36 hours over the lake.
Ocean Springs Police Department reported flash flooding in the Ocean Springs area, and calls to assist motorists in high water.
Broadcast media reported flash flooding from heavy rain in the Gulf Park Estates area.
Several small pine trees were uprooted and snapped in the Judy Dahl Road area north of Highway 24. Some trees had to be cleared from the roads in that area.

A weak tornado touched down along an intermittent track from the Cypress Lake area northeastward to just southwest of the community of Necaise. A few homes had minor roof damage, one home was shifted off its foundation. One home had a portion of siding roof peeled off, and a few trees were snapped or blown down. Most of the damage path was rated as WF0 with an isolated area of EF1 damage. Path length was 6 miles, path width 40 yards. Maximum winds were approximately 100 mph. Time of event was based on radar.

events.event_narrative: A cooperative observer estimated 50 mph winds. Strong rotation was noted on KLIX radar at 6500 feet, as thunderstorm approached island from Caminada Bay. No funnel clouds or waterspouts were observed.

events.event_narrative: SAWRS metar observation at KAXO reported a northwest wind gusting to 35 knots.
Public report of large hail southeast of Denham Springs received via social media.
Golfball size hail reported in Denham Springs via NWSChat.
Automated weather observation at Lakefront Airport reported a wind gust to 41 knots at 2012CST.
During a widespread power outage in the wake of Hurricane Isaac, several reports of heat exhaustion were reported, including one fatality from heat stroke.

The tornado initially touched down near the intersection of Highway 27 and Simon Road. The storm moved northeast causing sporadic EF-0 damage for a few miles roughly along Simon and Taylor Roads. Near the intersection of Simon and Allen Hill roads, the tornado destroyed a metal building and threw the debris 200 to 300 yards down it's path. The storm strengthened as it neared Highway 48, causing more significant damage. Two homes suffered moderate damage to a brick facade, and roofing and a dairy barn was destroyed near the crossing of Dexter Road and Highway 48. The tornado then crossed Highway 48 and continued to cause significant damage to trees with some minor damage to a few more structures. It also picked up several large hay bales and threw them 75 to 100 feet. The tornado began to weaken as it approached the Walthall/Marion County line, but did continue to cause damage for a few more miles into Marion County per survey results from WFO Jackson MS. Estimated maximum wind speed in Walthall County was 100 mph.

A weak tornado touched down a couple of times just south of Poplarville, causing minor property damage. A pool was overturned and minor damage was reported to a mobile home on Dupont Harts Chapel Road. A porch and an outbuilding were damaged at a residence on Highway 53. Path length was approximately 1.5 miles and path width was 20 yards. Maximum winds were estimated at 70 mph.

The tornado first touched down on Highway 61 near the intersection with the Baton Rouge Barge Canal. The tornado caused moderate damage to a roof of a single family residence and minor damage to a convenience store. A tree was uprooted at the same location. The tornado then traveled east-northeast, causing sporadic tree damage until it crossed over New Rafe Meyer Road and moved into the Lincoln Heights subdivision. This was the location of the worst damage with numerous softwood trees snapped and a few residences with moderate to major roof damage. A travel trailer was rolled over 25 to 30 yards and destroyed. The tornado then continued to travel to the east-northeast, crossing over Highway 19 and causing moderate damage to the roof of a car wash. Afterward, the tornado continued to the east-northeast, causing sporadic tree damage and minor roof damage to a few homes before finally lifting near the intersection of Plank Road and Dyer Road.
Trees were blown down along Cell Land and State Highway 1.
Numerous trees were blown down along Cane Market Road in Greenwell Springs.

A tornado touched down near the intersection of Airline Highway and Black Bayou Road. It ripped a metal roof off a boat dealership and shattered the windshield of 10 cars at a car dealership. An eyewitness also saw a small pickup truck lifted into the air about 20 feet and came back down on its wheels. The tornado tracked to the east along Black Bayou Road, causing sporadic tree damage and minor roof damage to a few residences. Before the tornado crossed Highway 44, it impacted a fire station, blowing in 2 large overhead doors, and blowing out 3 large overhead doors on the opposite side of the building. A nearby metal frame building was heavily damaged. The tornado continued to the east and lifted before reaching Ott Road. The maximum wind was estimated at 90 mph.
Metal roof damage was reported at a nursery in Bogalusa.

Trees were blown down along Millerville Road in the Tunica Hills area in Baton Rouge. This caused power outages to approximately 1000 Demco Electric Company customers. Type and size of trees were unknown.
A section of a metal roof on a school was peeled back. The location was near the intersection of Louisiana Highways 30 and 431.
A few trees were blown down on Sylvest Road. Time of the event was based on radar.
A few trees were blown down on Lake Choctaw Road.
Ponchatoula Police Department reported a large tree blown down and a power pole leaning over in Ponchatoula.
Hancock County EMA reported a waterspout 1 mile south of Long Beach.
Observation at Gulfport Outer Range station GPOM6.
A woman reported wind damage to her home to the local TV station. She reported that she saw rotation in the clouds outside her home after the event.

events.event_narrative: The tornado first touched down south of Highway 24, just east of the intersection of Highway 33 and Highway 24 on the south side of Centreville. Initially, numerous soft wood trees and a few hard woods were snapped and uprooted, and a few power poles lost their crossmembers. The tornado quickly moved to the east-northeast across Highway 24 uprooting another 6 to 10 trees, one of which clipped a house, bringing down much of the east facing wall. The tornado was 170-200 yards wide at this point and continued into the town of Centreville. A tire service station lost most of its canopy with the columns still standing, and the Centreville Head Start lost its metal awning.||The tornado crossed Fort Street with many more trees coming down, one on top of a car. Also along Fort Street, a single-wide mobile home lost most of its exterior walls. On East Howard Street, another tree fell into a house, pinning and injuring a lady. The tornado continued to the east-northeast, leading to another area of significant tree damage, uprooting and snapping numerous hard woods. A residence had minor structural damage leading to the carport partially collapsing. The tornado moved along Highway 48 for about another mile causing light tree damage before lifting. Times were based on radar and eyewitness reports. Maximum wind speed was estimated at 105 mph.

A large portion of a fence was blown down behind Wal-Mart and damage was reported to the roof of a car wash on Highway 90. Time of event estimated by radar.
Tree branches and power lines were reported down in Luling. Time of event was estimated by radar.
A photo from a local television news web sit showed a well defined waterspout associated with a supercell thunderstorm.
Scattered tree and large limb damage across the city of Zachary was due to straight line winds.

The tornado initially touched down on Harris Road on the southwest side of McNeil causing EF0 and EF1 damage, where it snapped several pine trees. It moved northeastward and rapidly intensified, resulting in a small area of upper range EF-2 and low end EF-3 damage along Joe Smith Road and Sones Chapel Road. The worst damage occurred when a single story brick veneer triplex dwelling was destroyed with only two small interior walls standing. The tornado weakened after crossing Highway 11, causing mainly tree and minor roof damage, until it re-intensified in the far northeast corner of Pearl River County near Red Hill church Road. It caused upper range EF-1 damage as it was leaving Pearl River County into Stone County. County officials preliminary estimate of 22 homes destroyed, 8 homes with major damage, 16 homes with minor damage and an additional 9 homes affected. Eight people were transported by EMS to area hospitals, although additional minor injuries likely occurred. Maximum winds in Pearl River County were estimated around 140 mph. This tornado continued to track northeast across several more counties in south Mississippi for a total path length of 61 miles. Event times were based on radar and eyewitness accounts.
Thunderstorm winds blew down trees on Sidney Road.
Several trees were blown down near Highway 421 in the area of Austin Road and at Whitestown Road at Delee Road. Trees were also down on Sage Hill Road with complete road blockage.
A tree was reported down on Highway 25 north of Clifton.
Trees were reported down on Highway 35.
A weak tornado touched down in Marrero near the intersection of Barataria and LaPalco Blvd. A gas station sign was blown over and minor damage was done to a fast food restraunt drive-through canopy.
