events.event_narrative: Observation at station KVKY.
A few roads were reported impassible due to high water from heavy rain.
Several roads in Gonzales were impassible due to high water from heavy rain. Water was approaching several homes.

A weak tornado touchdown touched down briefly at an industrial plant on Highway 405 east southeast of Plaquemine, LA.  Small area of roofing and some siding were pulled off a well constructed metal building. The tornado strength was estimated at upper end EF1 range with maximum wind speeds of 105 mph.
Street flooding was reported in Labadieville with water in one residence.
Widespread street flooding was reported in Livingston Parish, including Denham Springs with a number of roads closed due to high water.
Widespread street flooding was reported in Gonzales with numerous roads closed across the parish. Water was threatening several residences and businesses.

A storm survey determined sporadic damage in various locations near Franklinton. Damage at gravel company on Highway 16, on the south portion of Franklinton, a portion of the metal roof was peeled off and a few wood branches were snapped and blown to the northeast.

Damage was reported to a couple of homes in the Hackley community. One house had a roof blown off along with a portion of a wall damaged. Another house had major roof damage and damage to siding. Time of event was based on radar.

A storm survey determined a track with EF-0 type damage originating near the Zachary community park west of Highway 964, crossing into the Ravenwood Subdivision, then the Live Oak Trace Subdivision. Damage was mostly fencing knocked down and yard play equipment toppled in numerous yards. The tornado crossed Highway 64/Church Street, into a large open pasture, then lifted briefly over Zachary High School. Minor tree damage was noted along Highway 19 and along Highway 67 about 1 mile south of Port Hudson-Pride Highway. The storm continued northeast into East Feliciana Parish.

A storm survey determined that a tornado moved out of East Baton Rouge Parish into East Feliciana Parish along Highway 67. Significant tree damage was noted where the tornado crossed Highway 67 just east of the Comite River Bridge. Several large trees were snapped and a few hardwoods were uprooted. A detached carport was destroyed to the north of the highway. No other damage was detectable thereafter. The leftward curvature of the track would suggest that the tornadic storm was occluding while crossing Highway 67 over the Comite River Basin.

A storm survey confirmed a tornado touchdown. The tornado touched down on Progress Road just east of Interstate 59 and traveled approximately 1 mile. The path width was approximately 150 yards. Over one dozen hardwood and softwood trees were snapped, one of which severely damaged a pickup truck. A metal workshop building had significant roof damage in which half of it was removed. A trampoline was lifted and thrown approximately 200 yards. The damage was consistent with EF-1 intensity. Winds were estimated at 95 mph.
A public report of quarter size hail was relayed by Gloster Police Department.
Several trees were reported down near the intersection of Highways 48 and 45.
A tree was reported blown down on Whitestown Road in the Cornor area.
Quarter size hail was reported in the Angola area.
A lightning strike caused a power outage in Gramercy.
A lightning strike damaged one home in the Loranger area.
Widespread reports of power lines and trees down were received from the Bennett Bridge Road area to the Bush-Folsom Road area. Time of the event was estimated from radar.
A trained spotter reported quarter size hail in the city of Bogalusa.
A report of quarter size hail was received from the Hickory area.

A weak tornado touched down in the Mathews area and moved north on an intermittent path to near the intersection of US Highway 90 and Louisiana Highway 308. A few house canopies were damaged along with roof and fascia damage to a few structures. Fencing was knocked down at the high school and a HVAC unit was blown off a small building. Several power lines and power poles were knocked down on US Highway 90. Path length approximately 2 miles, and width 25 yards. EF0 rating with maximum wind 85 mph.

A weak tornado touched down on an intermittent path from Main Port Road near Industrial Road, extending northeast to the intersection of Grand Caillou Road and Industrial Boulevard. Several car windows were blown out and a small car turned over on Main Port Road. Several windows were broken at Chabert Medical Center along with several vehicle windows blown out. Several pieces of power equipment at the hospital were damaged. Two service stations on Grand Caillou Road had canopies damaged. Damage patch 1 mile, path width 30 yards, maximum wind 95 mph.
Golfball size hail was reported in the Gibson/Bayou Black area.
Quarter size hail was reported in Gray. The hail lasted 15 to 20 minutes. Report received on Facebook.
Received a report of quarter size hail in Des Allemands.
A photo posted on social media indicated oblong shaped hailstone in a person's hand with a size of about 2.25 to 2.50 inches.
Fire Station 86 near LaPalco Blvd and Westwood Drive reported golfball size hail.
Quarter size hail was reported in the Lower Garden District.
A NWS Cooperative Observer reported ping-pong ball size hail in Terrytown.
A NWS employee reported nickel size hail in Chalmette.
Quarter size hail reported in Galvez.
Golf ball size hail reported in Galvez.
The intersection of Three Rivers Road and Dedeaux Road was impassible due to flash flooding.
Heavy rain caused flash flooding in several areas of Jackson County including: Cook Road at Tucker Road, Van Cleave area, and the McClellan Road and Comstock Avenue area in Latimer.
A sheriff's deputy east of the Franklin County Line and Highway 567 reported golf ball size hail.

Thunderstorm wind gusts caused minor damage to a house under renovation on Highway 430 north-northeast of Franklinton.  A portion of the siding was peeled off, and roofing and insulation was blown in a northeast direction.
Broadcast media relayed a report from a police scanner of a tree down on Hampton Road in Wakefield. Event time estimated based on radar.
A few trees reported blown down and minor roof damage to one home in Oscar.
Several trees were reported blown down across Highway 68 near Wilson. Event time estimated based on radar.
Two large oak trees uprooted near Greenwell Springs Road about 1 mile south of Stoney Birch Point Road.
Limbs 4 inches in diameter were snapped.
Penny to dime size hail reported in Bogalusa.
Hail slightly larger than quarter size reported in Gonzales along Highway 44.
Power lines were reported down on several homes near New River Road and Highway 48 West in the Tylertown area.
Law enforcement received reports of multiple trees down across the west and north sides of Covington.
A National Weather Service employee relayed a report of quarter size hail halfway between Covington and Abita Springs.

events.event_narrative: A small piece of sheet metal was torn off a building at the NASA Michoud Facility, and minor tree damage was also reported. An 84 mph wind gust was recorded at the facility at 1105 am CDT with multiple wind gusts in the 50 to 60 mph range.

Hancock County Emergency Manager reported minor roof damage in the Kiln area. A peak wind gust of 60 mph was recorded at a radio station in Waveland at 1153 CDT. Also a wind gust of 53 mph was measured at a weather station at a casino in Bay St. Louis at 1146 CDT.

events.event_narrative: Louisiana Offshore Oil Port (LOPL1) reported a wind gust of 55.9 knots.
Gulfport Airport ASOS (KGPT) reported a wind gust of 52 knots or 60 mph.

Minor roof damage was reported with tin peeled off of at least one structure. Multiple trees were reported blown down across the county. Sand was blown across U.S. Highway 90 in several places. A private weather observation network reported measured peak wind gust of 76.5 mph at a casino in Biloxi at 1219 CDT, and 63.7 mph at a television station in Biloxi at 1209 CDT.

events.event_narrative: Several trees were blown down between Folsom and Covington.
A 58 mph wind gust measured at mid Lake Pontchartrain Causeway.

A weak tornado touched down about 3 miles southeast of Lacombe and continued on a fairly continuous path to 2 miles east of Slidell Airport. Several large trees were snapped or uprooted, large tree limbs were snapped and power lines were knocked down by fallen trees and limbs. Minor to moderate roof damage occurred to several houses, along with some siding blown off and fences blown down. Most of the damage was in the EF0 range with isolated low end EF1 damage. Estimated maximum path width 120 yards, estimated peak wind speed 88 mph.
Roof damage was reported to one home in Angie.
Power lines were blown down in Franklinton.
Several trees were blown down near the intersection of Highway 1072 and Highway 60.
A roof was blown off of a house in Pine.
Several trees were blown down on the west side of the town of Pearl River.
Several large trees were knocked down on 5th Avenue between 25th and 26th Streets. There was also some fencing in the same area that was blown down.
The Pointe Coupee Emergency Manager reported street flooding on several local streets including Highway 81 north of U.S. Highway 190. In addition, water was reported in a few homes on Romalice Drive.
A measured wind gust of 52 knots was recorded at Gulfport Airport.
Multiple trees and power lines were reported down along Cuevas-Delisle Road.

events.event_narrative: Grand Isle SAWRS reported a 63 mph wind gust. Winds appear to have been associated with a wake depression.
Lightning struck a Gulfport home during the early morning hours. One home was destroyed by the ensuing fire and a second home suffered minor damage to vinyl siding.

A short lived tornado touched down near the intersection of West Loyola Drive and Joe Yenni Boulevard. The storm moved nearly due south along West Loyola causing minor to moderate roof damage to about a dozen homes. The tornado also downed power lines, knocked over light poles, and ripped large limbs off of several large oak trees. A few of the limbs were upward of 18 inches in diameter. The tornado lifted shortly after crossing the intersection of West Loyola Drive and Vintage Drive. Sporadic straight line wind damage was also found in surrounding areas. Estimated peak wind speed was 90 mph.

A weak tornado touched down near the intersection of Meadowdale Street and Kent Avenue in Metairie, where it downed a large, but rotting, tree onto a parked car. The tornado moved southeastward causing minor roof damage to a few residences as it approached Veterans Boulevard. At the intersection of Transcontinental Drive and Veterans Boulevard, the tornado snapped several small trees and overturned a large truck, with the two occupants suffering minor injuries. The tornado continued to cause minor damage to trees and rooftops as it moved through the Pontchartrain Gardens subdivision. The tornado ripped a metal breezeway awning at a private school before crossing Interstate 10. It continued southeastward tearing large branches from trees and sporadically causing minor roof damage to several homes before lifting near the intersection of North Woodlawn Avenue and West Metairie Drive. Estimated peak wind was 75 mph.

A weak tornado touched down in the Bayou Paul area, just north of St. Gabriel. The short lived tornado crossed over Lawrence Parkway, Beehive Street, and Daisy Avenue, mainly causing tree damage. Five to ten oaks were snapped or uprooted with numerous branches snapped. One storage shed had a roof ripped off. The tornado quickly lifted after crossing Daisy Avenue. Estimated peak wind was 85 mph.
A few small trees were reported blown down in St. Gabriel.
A tree was blown down on Louisiana Highway 1148 just north of Plaquemine. Event time was estimated based on radar.
Wind gust of 51 knots or 59 mph was measured at New Orleans International Airport.
Structural damage reported in Mid-City.
Multiple large metal storage shed units blown over.
Metal awnings were torn apart at a car dealership off Jefferson Highway and Brooklyn Avenue.
A power pole was snapped at the intersection of St. Charles and St. Andrew.
Structural damage to new construction at the corner of Veterans Boulevard and Roosevelt Boulevard.
A metal warehouse door was blown in on Piedmont Street.
Five power poles were snapped on Acron Street.
Large limbs greater than 4 inches in diameter were snapped off trees along Idaho Street.
A metal frame patio was blown over on North Sibley Street.
A flagpole was snapped near Transcontinental Drive and West Metairie Avenue.
A tree was blown down along Washington Avenue between Jeff Davis and Broadway Street.
Thunderstorm wind gusts caused damage to a house roof, garage door, and outdoor shed. Several trees were also snapped.

Heavy rainfall of 7 to 8 inches resulted in flash flooding across portions of Jackson County. The Pascagoula Airport recorded slightly more than 7 inches of rain during the day. Many roadways and some homes were flooded. Emergency response crews rescued 20 people from flooded cars and 70 people were evacuated from Moss Point neighborhoods which flooded. Several residents were also rescued from flooded neighborhoods in Pascagaoula. In Gautier, two businesses and six homes flooded. Damage to county roads was estimated around $1.5 million.  ||Evacuations occurred in portions of Moss Point due to flooding of a bayou and drainage canals.
The Sun Herald newspaper reported quarter size hail in Gautier.

Heavy rain in Harrison County resulted in flash flood of roadways and low lying areas across east and southeast portions of the county.  Harrison County Emergency Manager reported that Road 106 off of Lamey Bridge was closed due to flash flooding, as well as Boney Avenue off of D'Iberville Boulevard. Daily rainfall of approximately 5 inches of rainfall was recorded at cooperative observer site near Biloxi.
The intersection of West Esplanade and East Loyola was impassible due to flash flooding. One vehicle was stalled due to water.
Numerous streets were reported flooded, especially around Audubon Subdivision.
Local broadcast media reported several streets in New Orleans were impassable due to flash flooding. Water was up to the doors of cars in some locations.
The Louisiana Association of Realtors building caught fire due to a lightning strike.
A tree was was blown down, blocking Highway 51 north of Interstate 10. Event time was based on radar.
A few tree limbs and power lines were blown down. Event time was estimated based on radar.
A 37 knots wind gust recorded at the NOAA C-Man station at Shell Beach.

events.event_narrative: A 38 knot wind gust was recorded at the NOAA C-Man station on Grand Isle.

A steel girder stick frame camp with vinyl siding and metal roof on a 15 foot pier was struck by thunderstorm wind gusts. Nearly the entire structure was blown to the east with roofing material and furniture blown 30 to 50 yards down wind. Two portions of siding were blown across Chef Menteur Highway about 10 yards east of the roadway. Two additional camp structures across the highway also had minor damage.
Quarter size hail was reported in Addis.
Quarter size hail was reported in the Westminster area.
A large tree was snapped in the St. Amant area.
A large tree was reported blown down on Choctaw Road.
Large tree limbs were downed by strong winds, blocking the roadway in the Broadmoor subdivision.
A 46 knot wind gust was recorded at Lakefront Airport.
Flooding was reported on Highway 68 and Highway 19 just northeast of Jackson.
Lightning started a fire in an empty house near Bayou Corne. The home was empty due to sink hole evacuations. Event time estimated based on radar.
An industrial service company just north northeast of Amelia had considerable roof damage to a couple of metal buildings. One building lost much of it's roof. Three power poles were also snapped.
Half dollar size hail was reported by an off duty NWS employee in the Indian Village subdivision.
A shed was blown down and roof damage to a residence was reported in Chackbay by the local fire department.
A few trees were reported blown down along Highway 307 in Chackbay.
Quarter size hail was reported along Duncan Street in Slidell.
Reports of quarter size hail were received from St. Rose.
Hail up to 1 inch in diameter was reported in Luling.
Trees were reported blown down along Magnolia Ridge Road and Old Spanish Trail in Boutte.
Numerous streets were flooded in Slidell with several cars stalled by the flood waters.
Quarter size hail was reported in Marrero.
DKCM6 C-MAN station reported a peak gust of 36 knots.
RARM6 C-MAN station reported a peak gust of 37 knots.
PTBM6 C-MAN station reported a peak gust of 34 knots.

events.event_narrative: A waterspout was observed and photographed near Grand Isle.
A trained spotter confirmed a waterspout about 8 miles northwest of Kenner over the western part of Lake Pontchartrain.
The augmented METAR observation from New Orleans International Airport reported a waterspout north of the observation point and moving northwest. The waterspout dissipated around 548 pm CDT.
D'Iberville police department reported several road closures in Forest Cove subdivision. Several public reports of flooding were received, including water in at least one home in D'Iberville.
The C-MAN station near Bay Waveland Yacht Club reported a measured thunderstorm gust of 34 knots.
A wind gust of 37 knots was reported at Lakefront Airport.

Several reports of flooding were received from the Slidell area, with numerous streets impassable, and water encroaching on homes. Some areas affected included the Gause Boulevard area, as well as Lake Village and Robert Park subdivisions.
Quarter size hail was reported in the Big Point community.
A storm spotter reported 60 mph winds in Biloxi with small tree limbs down.
Several trees were blown down and a few garage doors were damaged by thunderstorm wind gusts in the southeast portion of Baton Rouge.
Large tree limbs blown down at the Whispering Pines Golf Course in Hurley.
Lightning strikes damaged 5 golf carts, 3 chargers and a sprinkler system at Whispering Pines Golf Course in Hurley.
Approximately two dozen trees were reported blown down. One blocked U.S. Highway 51, and a few power lines were reported down in Fernwood. The event time was estimated based on radar.

events.event_narrative: A large tree was blown down onto a mobile home.
NOAA C-Man Station SHBL1 recorded a wind gust of 43 knots.
NOAA Station NWCL1 - New Canal Station recorded a wind gust of 44 knots.
Power lines were reported blown down in the D'Iberville area.

Very heavy rainfall of 5 to 7 inches occurred over several hour time period in southern Harrison County. At the Gulfport Airport, 4.65 inches of rain fell in one hour, and storm total rainfall was 6.06 inches.  Widespread flooding of streets and main roadways occurred across Gulfport, Biloxi and Orange Grove. In Gulfport, the flooding occurred along US Highways 90 and 49, along Pass Road, and near the Courthouse and Memorial Hospital areas. In Biloxi, the main flooding was along US Highway 90 from the Interstate 110 Loop to Biloxi Bay Bridge. At least 10 cars were stranded along Highway 90. Emergency management reported 15 to 20 houses had minor flooding.
A trained spotter reported 7 to 8 minutes of hail with some up to quarter size.
A 47 knot wind gust was measured at Lakefront Airport.

events.event_narrative: C-MAN station BURL1 reported a 41 mph wind gust.
Minor coastal flooding was reported on Lakeshore Drive near Canal Street and the Mardi Gras Fountain.
Minor tidal flooding was reported along Lakeshore Drive in Mandeville.
Broadcast media provided pictures of snow in St. Francisville with one tenth inch accumulation through social media.

McComb Police Department reported one half inch of snow. One bridge was closed due to icing and two other bridges beginning to ice over. A local resident reported four tenths of an inch of snow at Southwest Mississippi Community College in Summit.
A local resident sent in a picture of one half inch accumulation of snow in Woodville.
A local resident relayed a report of one half to one inch of snow in Port Allen.
A local resident relayed a report of one quarter inch of snow in Tylertown.
A local resident relayed a report of just under one half inch of snow in Amite.
A local resident relayed a report of two tenths of an inch of snow in Poplarville.
A trained spotter reported just under an inch of snow in 30 minutes about 5 miles northwest of Baton Rouge.
A local resident reported heavy sleet in Metairie with overpasses beginning to ice.
A local resident reported a heavy sleet and light snow mix for 45 minutes in Laplace at the Interstate 10 and Interstate 55.
A mixture of light freezing rain and sleet fell across the parish with light icing reported on exposed objects and bridges. A few light snow reports were also received.
A mixture of light rain, light freezing rain and sleet occurred. Some elevated roadways and bridges had icing.
A mixture of light rain, light freezing rain and sleet occurred across the county. Icing was reported on elevated roadways.
Light Sleet and occasional light freezing rain was reported across the parish.

The parish emergency manager reported about one half inch accumulation of snow and sleet overnight across Pointe Coupee Parish. Icing was reported on bridges and roads, with sleet going on at the time of the report.

The parish emergency manager estimated about one half inch of sleet and snow accumulation across the parish overnight. An isolated report of one and a half inches was received from Darlington. Sleet was falling at the time of the report.

The parish emergency manager reported one half to three quarter inch of sleet and snow accumulation overnight across the parish. Icing was reported on bridges and roads. Sleet was occurring the time of the report.
A local resident reported an inch of snow in Centreville.
A mix of sleet and snow was reported in Golden Meadow.
Freezing rain was occurring just north of Biloxi with ice forming on the elevated portion of Interstate 110.
Freezing rain was beginning to accumulate in Independence. Vehicles were stopping on the side of the road to clear windshields and free wipers.
Sleet reported at Galliano Airport.
Most of Pike County reported one and a half inches of sleet with locally higher amounts.
Around two inches of sleet was reported in Tylertown. An additional inch of snow fell on top of the sleet.

Snow and sleet was beginning to accumulate in Kentwood. A local resident reported that sleet was just beginning to accumulate in Roseland.  Heavy sleet was reported in Kentwood with approximately an inch of sleet accumulation.
The parish emergency manager reported that sleet was beginning to fall in Thibodaux.
A local resident reported that sleet was beginning to accumulate in Houma.
Reports of sleet accumulations approaching an inch were received from the Liberty area. There was a light coating of ice on limbs and power lines.
One half inch to two inches of sleet, snow, and freezing rain was reported across much of West Feliciana Parish.
A combined inch of sleet and freezing rain was reported in Centreville.
Three quarters of an inch of sleet was reported in Ethel. A local resident reported freezing rain and sleet producing light accumulations in Slaughter.
A light glaze was reported developing on power lines in Metairie.
One tenth of an inch of sleet and freezing rain was reported in Gramercy.
The parish emergency manager reported one inch of sleet accumulation across the northern portion of Washington Parish.  One half inch of sleet was reported in Franklinton.
One half inch of sleet accumulation was reported at the Emergency Operations Center in Greensburg.

A National Weather Service Employee reported three tenths of an inch of sleet and two tenths of an inch of freezing rain at his home in Slidell.  One half inch of combined sleet and freezing rain accumulation was reported in the town of Pearl River.  One half inch of sleet and freezing rain was reported in Mandeville. Around three tenths of an inch of sleet was reported in Abita Springs.

Sleet accumulations were near one half inch. One quarter inch of ice was covering all roads in Autumn Run and Collins Place subdivisions. All precipitation was freezing on contact. Ice glazed trees and power lines along Louisiana Route 447. One half inch accumulation was also reported in Denham Springs by a CoCoRAHS observer. A Livingston Parish resident reported three quarters of an inch of sleet and freezing rain accumulation 10 miles north of Walker.
One half inch of sleet was reported just south of McNeil and three tenths of an inch of sleet and ice was reported just south of Picayune.
Sleet accumulations ranging from one quarter to three quarters of an inch were reported across the city of Pascagoula. There were significant issues with icing of roads and bridges.
A resident of Laplace reported just under one quarter inch of sleet.
One quarter of an inch of sleet was reported in Pride.
One inch of sleet fell on top of one quarter inch of freezing rain in St. Martin.

A weak tornado touched down in the vicinity of Mississippi Highway 48 and Piggott-Easterling Road. Several large pine trees were uprooted, and large tree branches were snapped. A house roof was damaged by a fallen tree. Damage path was one half mile, path width was 40 yards. The tornado was rated EF0 with an estimated maximum wind of 85 mph. Time of the tornado was estimated based on radar.
Flooding was reported at two businesses at Baldwin Street and South Lamar Street.|An elderly couple was rescued from floodwaters in the Fernwood Flats area.
A wind gust of 59 mph was reported by a television station at Benson Towers near the Superdome.
Broadcast media relayed a report of a 65 mph wind gust at the St. Bernard Government Center in Chalmette. The event time was based on radar.
A few trees were reported blown down in West Feliciana Parish north of St. Francisville.
An eight foot box culvert was washed out on David Allen at Joe Smith Road. Several homes in northern St. Helena Parish also had minor flooding. Time was estimated by radar.
Shell Beach NOAA CMAN station recorded a 42 knot wind gust.

Several houses experienced thunderstorm wind damage in Meraux, primarily along Judy Drive. Damage was mainly to roofing material removed. A few windows were blown out, a door was blown in, and fencing blown down. A few large tree limbs were also snapped.

Several houses in the Violet area experienced thunderstorm wind damage, primarily along 6th Street. The primary damage was shingles and roofing material being removed. Several fences were also blown down.
Hail up to half dollar size was reported in Prairieville by the fire department.
Hail up to the size of quarters was reported south of Belle Chasse.
Penny size hail was reported in Baton Rouge.
Pea to penny sized hail reported near the corner of Tiger Bend Road and Antioch Road.
Freezing rain caused icing on Interstate 110, as well as the Mississippi River Bridge on Interstate 10. The icing was responsible for multiple accidents in these areas.
Light icing was observed on signs and trees in the Walker area.
Freezing rain with light icing was reported on trees and bridges throughout the parish according to the Sheriff's Office dispatcher.
Icing was reported on bridges on Mississippi Highways 48 and 584 in southern Amite County.
Icing was reported on the Homochitto Bridge on U.S. Highway 61 in northern Wilkinson County.
Several pine trees and large live oak branches were reported downed in the River Oaks Subdivision along Indian Village Road. Event time was estimated based on radar.

Torrential rainfall of 5 to 8 inches fell across northern Wilkinson County and extreme northwest Amite County.  Approximately 78 homes and 1 business in Wilkinson County were affected by flooding, with 28 of those homes receiving major damage.  The area around Crosby and Silver Creek community experienced the greatest impact from flooding. Five people were trapped by flood waters in the Silver Creek area and rescued around 815 am.
Torrential rainfall of 5 to 8 inches fell across northwest Amite County. Several homes were impacted in the Crosby area and several roads in the northwest part of the Amite County were flooded.

Rainfall of 3 to 5 inches produced widespread street flooding in and around Slidell. Some sections of roads were impassable to low profile vehicle due to one to two feet of water. Some vehicles were stranded according to reports from television, radio, print media and social media sites.
Two homes were reported flooded on Rue Charlemagne in east Slidell.
Quarter size hail was reported in the Holmesville area.
A garage door was blown onto a road in Holmesville.
Pea to dime size hail was reported in Gray.
Roofing was blown off of a shed due to strong thunderstorm winds east of Wilmer.
Golf ball size hail was reported near Old Hammond Highway and Jefferson Highway in Baton Rouge.
Over 20 trees were snapped and uprooted along East Domiano Lane. The NWS storm survey determined that the damage was from straight line winds.
Winds were estimated at 65 to 75 mph around the Sherwood Forest Subdivision. A roof was blown off an apartment complex at the intersection of Little John and Florida.

events.event_narrative: The Pike County Emergency Manager reported several trees blown down in and around McComb. A tree fell on an apartment building, damaging it and injuring an occupant. A tree fell on a home and produced moderate damage to the home. Trees and power lines were blown down across the county. Pea size hail was also reported.

An older model single wide trailer sustained moderate damage from an apparent rear flank downdraft event on Old Joe Moran Road near Kiln. The front porch was dislocated and blown over the trailer. Debris was blown 50 to 100 yards downrange. Two pine trees snapped at 15 feet across the road west of the trailer. Considerable damage was done to the interior of the trailer with objects lodged in the walls. The trailer was strapped down, but moved 6-8 inches on cinders. All windows were broken. Winds were estimated at 65-70 mph.

A storm survey determined that straight line winds estimated between 75 and 80 mph struck the Santa Rosa RV Resort Marina at 5800 Moss Bluff Road. Twenty RV trailers were overturned, with one rolled uphill. Several trees were topped along with large live oak limbs broken. Two stucco veneer walls on an apartment structure collapsed. Two individuals were extracted from one trailer that was destroyed and were hospitalized for moderate injuries. Event time was estimated by storm relative motion data from KLIX and KMOB radars.
A mixture of light rain and light freezing rain occurred across the metro area. Some elevated bridges had ice accumulation.
A mixture of light rain, light freezing rain and sleet occurred across Hancock County.  Some icing occurred on bridges and elevated roadways.

One to three inches of sleet, snow, and freezing rain was reported across much of West Feliciana Parish.

Water was estimated to be 12 to 18 inches deep. The incident occurred between 1000-1100CST.  Flooding began mid-morning with the event time estimated. A mesocyclone embedded in the squall line produced a tornado that initially touched d down along a gravel driveway near Derrick Street north of Pierre Part, snapping off large branches along the driveway, producing EF-0 damage. Path width was 50 yards wide at this point. The tornado moved east-southeast and crossed Derrick Street, damaging several homes and snapping hardwood trees. A carport was destroyed on one residence and a porch collapsed on another home. A third home had most of the tin roofing torn off the back of the house. The tornado was rated at EF-1 with a path width of 150 yards. The tornado continued east-southeast, crossing Louisiana Highway 70, paralleling Lee Drive, causing sporadic tree damage along the path and causing minor damage to homes, rating EF-0. The tornado re-intensified to EF-1 near the intersection of Lee Drive and East Drive. A chimney collapsed on one home and another home had a large portion of the tin roof removed with beams exposed. Several large trees were snapped at the base. The width remained 150 yards as it crossed Avoca Island Cutoff Canal, but the tornado weakened back to EF-0 strength as it crossed Grand Coupe Lane. A metal warehouse building had its doors blown inward at this location. The tornado moved into the woods near the end of Noe street where large branches were snapped off. The tornado was still 150 yards wide at this point. No access was available beyond this point, and it is unknown if the tornado remained on the ground beyond the end of Noe Street.

A mesocyclone embedded in the squall line produced another tornado initially touching down in an area of softwood pine trees west of Bayouside Street. Trees had large branches snapped, and EF-0 damage was noted. The path width was only 25 yards at this point. The tornado then moved to the southeast and crossed Louisiana Highway 402 causing additional EF-0 damage. Several trees had large branches snapped off, and a few trees were uprooted. No visible damage to any structures was noted.  The path width in this area was approximately 75 yards wide. The tornado crossed Louisiana Highway 1 and Bayou Lafourche just south of Hospital Road, causing additional tree damage. The tornado then crossed Louisiana Highway 308 south of Dodge Road, where additional tree damage in the form of large branches removed from hardwood trees was noted. All of this damage was rated EF-0, and the path width narrowed to 25 yards. No damage was noted beyond this point.

Another embedded mesocyclone embedded in the squall line produced a tornado. Tree damage was noted across a field west of Louisiana Highway 20, and due to lack of road access, this was determined to be the start point of the tornado. Several large trees were uprooted along the tree line. Damage was noted as EF-1 in this location. The tornado then moved east-southeast across the field, and crossed Louisiana Highway 20 at the intersection with Appletree Drive. EF-1 damage was noted here, and the tornado was approximately 75 yards wide at this point. A small professional building had large portions of siding ripped off and shingles missing from the roof. Trees were uprooted in varying directions in front of the home, and several power poles were snapped at the base in this location. The tornado then moved east-southeast down Appletree Lane and removed a large portion of the shingles from several homes. Several trees were also uprooted and snapped in this area. High end EF-0 and low end EF-1 damage was noted along Appletree Drive. At the end of Appletree Drive, a detached garage collapsed. The tornado then continued into the woods where a path was noted for several more yards with trees uprooted and snapped. The tornado remained 75 yards wide and maintained EF-1 strength as it moved into the woods. It is unknown if the tornado continued further into the woods due to a lack of access.

A mesocyclone embedded in the squall line produced a weak tornado. Small trees were uprooted in a field west of Louisiana Highway 306, producing EF-0 damage. Path width was 25 yards wide at this point. The tornado quickly moved to the east-southeast and crossed Highway 306 between Mark and Matthew Streets, where additional large tree branches were snapped from numerous trees. Minor damage to roof coverings was noted along Mark and Matthew Streets. Power poles were also leaning south of Matthew Street. The damage path was 50 yards wide at this point and EF-0 damage was noted. The tornado continued east-southeast, and moved across Shamrock Drive at Edna Street. A home had siding removed and some shingles removed. Trees were also damaged along Edna Street. The tornado was 50 yards wide and produced EF-0 damage along Edna and Shamrock Streets. There was additional tree damage observed beyond the levee behind Shamrock Street, but due to lack of access, this is where the end point of the tornado is noted.

A weak tornado., along the leading edge of a squall line,  touched down at the levee of Duncan Canal north of West Esplanade Avenue. Two wooden power poles were bent near an apartment complex. The storm tracked to the east-southeast with mainly light tree damage, and one area of light roof damage on Grandlake Boulevard. The tornado then crossed Canal Number 17, and lifted the roof off of the back porch of a house on Tulane Drive. On the opposite side of Tulane Drive, another house had a small portion of its roof ripped off. The tornado continued to the east-southeast and crossed West Louisiana State Drive and bent over one wooden power pole, and snapped a second one. The tornado then uprooted a hardwood tree in front of a house on West Loyola. The most significant damage occurred at the corner of Loyola and West Esplanade, where multiple wooden power poles and a few trees were snapped. The tornado then quickly lifted as it crossed West Esplanade. In addition to the tornado, sporadic light tree damage occurred south of the track. A large portion of the facade of a hotel on the corner of Loyola and the Interstate 10 Service Road was damaged due to straight line winds.
Trees were blown down in several areas of Pointe Coupee Parish. Three houses and two vehicles were damaged by fallen trees. Event time was estimated from radar.

Trees and power lines were blown down in many communities in Assumption Parish. Some homes received roof damage. The most concentrated damage was in the Napoleonville and Paincourtville areas. Event time estimated from radar.
Trees were reported down in multiple locations across Iberville Parish.
Numerous trees were reported blown down near Julia Road.
The front door was blown off of a commercial business on Choctaw Drive.
Several trees were reported blown down in the Houma area.
Trees and power lines were blown down in Bayou Gauche, Paradis and Des Allemands areas. Power poles were snapped along Louisiana Highways 306 and 632. Event time estimated.
Several trees and power poles were blown down by thunderstorm winds. Event time was estimated by radar.
A wind gust to 61 knots was measured at New Orleans Armstrong Airport.
A COOP observer recorded a 66 mph wind gust.

Eleven large railcar shipping containers were blown off a train on the east bank approach to the Huey P Long Bridge in the Elmwood area of Metairie. The tracks at the location of the damage were approximately 70 feet above the ground.
A few trees were reported down and some awnings blown off buildings at Belle Chasse Naval Air Station. A few trees and large branches were also blown down in areas just east of the Naval Air Station.
A trained spotter reported a 62 mph wind gust and a wall cloud in the Tiger Bend Road area. A large tree was also reported blown down onto an apartment building in the tiger bend area.
A spotter reported roof damage to a commercial building in Denham Springs.

events.event_narrative: Approximately 10 power poles were damaged along Louisiana Highway 1 south of Port Allen. Event time estimated by radar.

Large tree branches and isolated trees were blown down in scattered areas across the Baton Rouge, including areas around the LSU campus.  A man was injured when a tree fell onto the automobile he was driving.
Thunderstorm wind gusts downed large limbs and trees in several communities in Ascension Parish. Four homes were damaged by fallen trees. Several yard fences were also blown down.
Large tree limbs and one large tree were blown down by thunderstorm wind gusts.
Several power poles were blown down by thunderstorm winds.
The Tangipahoa Parish Sheriff's office reported a tree blown down by thunderstorm winds along Louisiana Highway 40 in Independence.
The Pike County Sheriff's Office reported a tree was knocked down by thunderstorm winds in Summit.
The Pointe Coupee Parish Emergency Manager reported that several trees were blown down by thunderstorm winds on Jack Torres Road.
The Pointe Coupee Parish Emergency Manager reported that several trees were blown down by thunderstorm winds on Louisiana Highway 976 near Livonia.
Numerous trees were reported damaged in the vicinity of Oldmixon Road north of Picayune.
A large tree limb was snapped off by thunderstorm winds and damaged a garage in Hammond.
Local television station meteorologists relayed photos of a large waterspout over Lake Pontchartrain near the Lake Pontchartrain Causeway.
The Harrison County Emergency Manager reported that southern Shaw Road just north of Mississippi Highway 53 was closed due to flash flooding.
An observer for the Harrison County Emergency Management office reported 8.41 inches of rain for the day northwest of Lyman.
Mississippi Highway 43 in northwest Hancock County was impassable due to water over the roadway. Several other roads in the general area were also closed due to high water.

A tornado touched down near Sibley Road about 1/4 mile east of Woodhaven Road, uprooting two hardwood trees. The track continued north-northwest with damage increasing significantly once the tornado reached Joel McDonald Road. On the far east and south side of the road, two houses had damage to their metal roofs with several sections missing. Barns and sheds in the yards of those homes were no longer intact. A metal roof from one of the sheds was found in a tree just above power line height. Across the street from these two homes were two mobile homes, both parallel to Joel McDonald Road. One mobile home was rolled onto its roof and the other was pushed off its blocks. Both were strapped down, with some straps snapping while others remained attached to the anchors which were uprooted. The tornado continued north-northwest toward Gene McDonald Road. Several trees were uprooted near homes on that road. Front and back porches on two mobile homes were lifted and thrown approximately 30 yards. One mobile home had a 3 foot by 6 foot hole in an exterior wall blown from the inside out. Two sheds were destroyed. The tornado lifted after uprooting two trees near Miller Lane Road. One was on the west side, the other on the east side of the road. One of those trees hit a pickup truck. Maximum wind speed was estimated at 110 mph.
Local broadcast media relayed a report from the public of dime to quarter size hail at Interstate 110 and Chippewa Road.
Standing water was reported on the middle and inside lanes of westbound Interstate 12 in Walker.

A tornado touched down on the east bank of the Mississippi River, damaging a pier at the foot of Williams Boulevard and snapping hardwood trees. The highest EF-1 damage occurred at the start of the tornado track from the Mississippi River to along Reverend Richard Wilson Drive with structural damage reported to homes and a business. The tornado continued to track northwest to Kenner Avenue, where it caused part of a roof to peel back on a single family home. The tornado then weakened to EF-0 as it lifted on the north side of the railroad tracks. Estimated peak wind was 110 mph.
Strong thunderstorm winds downed multiple trees onto a mobile home off Hooper Road in Greenwell Springs.
The LSU Ben Hur observation site measured a peak one minute wind of 59 mph and a peak gust of 69 mph.
A tree blown down by thunderstorm winds caused damage to an above ground swimming pool. Event time was estimated by radar.
A 68 mph wind gust was measured at the mid-lake point on the Lake Pontchartrain Causeway by Weatherflow equipment.
A tree was blown down across East 31st Street near Lee Road.
The WVUE television station measured a wind gust of 59 mph during a thunderstorm.
The Shell Beach CMAN station recorded a 51 mph wind gust during a thunderstorm.
Trees were reported blown down in Luling. The event time was estimated by radar.
Trees were reported blown down by thunderstorm winds in Ama. The event time was estimated from radar.
Orleans Parish Emergency Management reported extensive street flooding in New Orleans Lakeview, Lakefront and Mid City areas with some streets impassible.
Thunderstorm wind gusts damaged two large electrical transmission towers. Several trees were also blown down just northwest of Plaquemine.
Several trees and large limbs blown were down in scattered locations in New Orleans.
Several public reports and emergency management inspection indicate a weak tornado touched down in the Bayous Pigeon area overturning one mobile home and damaging several others.

Significant and deep street street flooding was reported by the public, state transportation agency and social media in various parts of Baton Rouge including the following streets: North Street, College Drive, Sherwood Forest Blvd, Goodwood Drive, and Perkins Road.

events.event_narrative: Minor flooding was reported at high tide of several streets east of Mississippi Highways 603 and 43 in the Shoreline Park area.
A tree was uprooted and a power pole was blown down by thunderstorm winds near the Louisiana State University campus. The event time was estimated by radar.
The 1108TH TASMG at Gulfport Airport had damage to generators, Humvees and maintenance platforms.
A tree was blown down and blocked both lanes of traffic at Mississippi Highway 53 and CC Camp Road.
A tree was blown down blocking one lane of traffic near Wolf River Road and Cable Bridge Road.

In the Bluebonnet Road and Jefferson Highway area, at least one vehicle was flooded out with occupants rescued, and water reported in at least one structure. Flooding was also reported on the Jefferson Highway and Airline Highway area and on Sherwood Forest and Coursey Blvd.
A few trees were reported blown down by thunderstorm winds between Pine and Franklinton.

events.event_narrative: Wind gust of 38 knots or 44 mph was recorded at Lakefront Airport (KNEW).
Wind gust of 56 knots or 64 mph was measured at McComb MS Lewis Field (KMCB).
Several trees were reported blown down in the city of McComb, and in areas just south and east of the city. Several of the trees blown down in the city brought down power lines and light poles.
A tree was reported blown down on a home just east of Baker.
Trees were reported blown down by thunderstorm winds along Muse Road south of Greensburg.
Several trees were reported blown down near Louisiana Highway 37 at Louisiana Highway 449 south of Greensburg.
A tree was reported blown down and blocking the right lane on Interstate 55 southbound near Mile Marker 39.
A report of golf ball size hail was received from Livonia via an Internet storm report submittal.
Two large trees were reported blown down by thunderstorm winds.
Wind gust of 49 mph or 43 kt was recorded at Lakefront Airport (KNEW).
Wind gust of 47 mph or 41 knots was recorded at Shell Beach NOAA C-MAN Station.

Bootheville ASOS (KBVE) recorded wind gust of 39 knots or  45 mph.

Along Cane Market Road, trees were reported snapped and siding was removed from several mobile homes. One tree fell on a vehicle. Event time was estimated by radar.
A large oak tree was blown down, blocking a driveway on Arnold Road. Event time was estimated by radar.
At the intersection of Courtney Road and Corbin Road, two pine trees were snapped off and one oak tree snapped by thunderstorm winds. Event time was estimated by radar.

Several trees were reported blown down in an area on the east side of False River along with a few signs and fences. Trees were also reported blown down in several other areas of Pointe Coupee Parish. Event time was estimated by radar.
A 44 knot wind gust was measured at Lakefront Airport. Wind gusts of 34 knots or higher were recorded from 1659 CDT through 1743 CDT.
A small pine tree was snapped or split, a small shed destroyed, and shingles blown off the roof of a residence on Mississippi Highway 569 south of Liberty.
Wind gust of 44 knots or 51 mph was recorded at Lakefront Airport (KNEW).
Station PTBM6 at Petit Bois Island reported a wind gust of 44 mph.

Weatherflow site XPTN at the mid point of the Lake Pontchartrain Causeway measured a wind gust of 65 mph. Temperature dropped 19 degrees from 92 degrees to 73 degrees in a few minutes with a thunderstorm passage.
Shell Beach C-MAN station reported a 58 mph wind gust.
Lakefront Airport reported a 54 mph wind gust.
The New Canal C-MAN station reported a 50 mph wind gust.
The Boothville ASOS reported a wind gust to 48 mph.
Power lines and trees were reported blown down in Golden Meadow. Power outages were reported from Golden Meadow to Grand Isle according to Jefferson Parish EM.
A shed was blown apart and trees blown down near Liberty. Several other trees were blown down around the county.
Lightning struck a crude oil storage tank batter located east of Liberty, that  became engulfed and had to be extinguished by local volunteer fire departments.

events.event_narrative: The C-MAN station in South Timbalier Block 52 reported a wind gust of 40 mph with a line of thunderstorms.
A trained spotter measured a 59 mph wind gust with a handheld anemometer in Hammond.
Part of the roof was blown off a mobile home on Red Hill Road near Independence.
Automated weather station at the Hammond Airport (KHDC) recorded a wind gust of 51 knots or 59 mph.
Trees were reported blown down at the intersection of Louisiana Highway 40 and Fitzgerald Church Road.
Quarter sized hail reported in Addis.
The Walthall County Sheriff's Office reported numerous trees blown down and power outages across the entire county. Most of the damage was reported in the Salem area.
The Pearl River County Sheriff's Department reported numerous trees blown down and power outages across the county, with most of the damage across northern portions of the county.
A 62 mph wind gust was reported at Waveland Yacht Club.
Hancock County Sheriff's Department reported numerous trees down along with power outages across much of the county.
A 50 knot wind gust was reported at Grand Pass station GRPL1.
A 41 knot wind gust was reported at Northeast Bay Gardene station BGNL1.
Hail just smaller than golfball size was reported along Yankee Town Road and Armes Road south of Saucier.
Multiple large tree limbs were blown down and power outages occurred south of Saucier.
Multiple trees were reported blown down along Mississippi Highway 603 north of Kiln.

Jackson County Emergency Management personnel reported 21 homes with minor flooding, at least seven businesses were flooded, and 14 families were being sheltered after flash flooding in the Pascagoula and Moss Point areas. As much as 5 to 8 inches of rain was reported across eastern Jackson County, with much of the rain falling between 330 pm and 530 pm CDT.
NOAA C-Man Station at Shell Beach recorded a wind gust of 45 knots or 51 mph.

An elderly woman was injured when her mobile home was shifted from the foundation on Kennedy Street. There was also minor damage to trees and an apartment complex car port. The tornado touched down after crossing the river near River Road and moved to the north-northwest for 0.75 miles. The maximum estimated winds were 80 mph. The time of the tornado was estimated by radar.

A weak tornado crossed Bayou Dularge and Louisiana Highway 315 about 8.9 miles southwest of the community of Theriot. Minor roof damage occurred to a few homes and sheet metal roof panels were pulled from roofs of storage buildings. Four medium sized boats were overturned in Bayou Dularge. Maximum winds were estimated at 75 mph. Damage path was approximately 150 yards long and 50 yards wide.
Thunderstorm winds downed large tree limbs.
The roof was ripped off a home near Chauvin Bridge.
Strong winds blew a tree on a home east of New Roads, and a road was blocked in the same area when another tree fell on the roadway.
A large tree was blown down on US Highway 190 in Lacombe between 9th and 12th Streets. The tree struck and damaged two occupied vehicles, but no injuries were sustained.

One foot inundation was reported in several areas on Bayou Liberty Road. Also, the entrance to Palm Lakes Subdivision was blocked by the Slidell Police Department due to minor flooding of roadways. Minor to moderate flooding of roadways was also reported along the Mandeville lakefront.
Several roads were closed due to high water over the western portion of Pike County between McComb and the Amite County line.

The tornado initially touched down just west of Hoover Road, snapping a tree and moved to the northeast. Before reaching Hoover Road, numerous large tree limbs were broken, a barn lost numerous roof panels, and several undercarriage panels of a modular home were ripped off. Sheet metal panels were strewn across the area for about 200 to 300 yards. After crossing Hoover Road, another large tree was snapped and another uprooted. The tornado then crossed US Highway 190 and crossed over Edna Kinchen Road. This location had the most significant tree damage with multiple softwoods and hardwoods snapped and uprooted. The tornado then moved into a field along Crain Road before causing some very light tree limb damage and minor roof damage to a mobile home. The tornado then continued to the northeast, crossing over Hutchinson Cemetary Road causing minor roof damage to another modular house, scattered limb damage, and knocked down a large section of a wood fence.

The tornado touched down along Mayers Road where a large tree was uprooted with minor damage to the undercarriage of a modular house, as well as sporadic large tree limb damage. The tornado continued into a wooded area crossing over the Tangipahoa River and Louisiana Highway 443. The tornado continued to the east leading to the most significant damage along Averett Road. Multiple metal sheds were destroyed. A large metal carport was ripped off, peeling some of the roof of a modular home off with it. Portions of this carport were thrown over 250 yards. Power lines were knocked down, along with one snapped tree, and multiple tree limbs down. A trampoline was also thrown 200-300 yards. The tornado continued to the east, crossing over Bailey Loop Road, leading to additional tree damage and one uprooted softwood tree. In addition, multiple smaller metal sheds were destroyed with the metal being carried 100-150 yards. The tornado lifted at Louisiana Highway 445.

Scattered thunderstorm wind damage was reported in the vicinity of Louisiana Highway 21 and Pierce Road near the community of Sun. Several large tree limbs were snapped,  one small tree was blown down, and minor wind damage occurred to a mobile home.

A tornado touched down just west of Mississippi Highway 53 and south of Mcneil-Mchenry Road in Pearl River County. Near where the tornado touched down, an outbuilding was destroyed and tree limbs were downed. As the tornado tracked east-northeast, more tree limbs were downed and a few wooden power poles and trees were snapped. Shortly after travelling east of Highway 53, a mobile home and outbuilding were damaged. Additional tree damage continued farther east-northeast before the tornado lifted.
Roof and structural damage was reported to a residence north of Picayune.

Isolated wind damage was noted in an area from approximately 5 miles west of Mcneil to just northwest of Mcneil. Damage consisted primarily of a few downed large tree limbs. Minor roof damage was also reported to a mobile home by emergency management. Event time was estimated based on radar.
Tides of 2 to 4 feet above normal tide levels resulted in moderate flooding of roadways across southern Terrebonne Parish and many roads were inundated.
Tides of 2 to 3 feet above normal tide levels resulted in moderate flooding of low lying terrain and roadways outside of the hurricane protection levees.
Tides of 2 to 4 feet above normal tide levels resulted in widespread flooding of low lying terrain and roadways including in the Lafitte and Barataria communities.
Tides of 2 to 3 feet above normal tide levels resulted in moderate flooding of low lying terrain and roadways outside of the hurricane protection levees.

Tides of 2 to 3 feet above normal tide levels resulted in moderate flooding of low lying terrain and roadways outside of the hurricane protection levees, including areas around Lake Pontchartrain. Flooding was reported on US Highways 11 and 90 in far east New Orleans.
Tides of 2 to 3 feet above normal tide levels resulted in moderate flooding of low lying terrain and roadways around Lakes Pontchartrain. Flooding was reported on US Highway 51.
Tides of 2 to 4 feet above normal tidal levels produced moderate flooding of low lying terrain and roadways in coastal Hancock County.
Tides of 1 to 3 feet above normal tidal levels produced minor to moderate flooding of low lying terrain and roadways in coastal areas.
Tides of 1 to 3 feet above normal tidal levels produced minor to moderate flooding of low lying terrain and roadways in coastal areas.

The Lafourche Parish Emergency Manager reported that a tin awning was blown from a trailer, severing a power line and landing on an adjacent home on Landreau Drive off Louisiana Highway 307 in the Kraemer area. Event time estimated by radar.
A public report of nearly AA battery sized hail fell in Sorrento.

A NWS storm survey confirmed an EF-1 tornado with winds estimated at 100 mph. The tornado began near US Highway 190 and Woodside Drive around 253 am and traveled northeast. An 18 wheeler was flipped and a trailer was re-positioned along with a metal roof ripped off a building. A door to the same building was blown inward. The tornado lifted near Cane Market Road and Blount Lane.

A NWS storm survey confirmed an EF-1 tornado with winds estimated at 100 mph. The tornado began around 320 am near Dupont Construction Road and US Highway 61. The tornado continued northeastward across Highway 61, Several wooden power poles along Highway 61 were snapped, and roof and fence damage occurred at the corner of Lee Drive and Jefferson Street. The tornado continued northeast into a wooded area behind the subdivision before lifting.
A tree was blown down in the Magnolia Oaks Subdivision near Prairieville.
Part of a roof was blown off of a trailer in Larose.
Siding and roof damage was reported to an elevated home in Barataria. Event time was estimated based on radar.
A NWS storm survey found straight line wind damage with power lines blown down at Fish Hatchery Road and Sandy Road near Lacombe.
Two power poles were blown down by thunderstorm winds near Louisiana Highway 23 and Adam Drive in the Jesuit Bend area.
A 51 knot wind gust was recorded at the Belle Chase Naval Air Station (KNBG).
A NWS storm survey found straight line wind damage with tree limbs and power lines blown down at US Highway 49 and West Wortham Road.

events.event_narrative: KMIS AWOS reported a peak gust of 47 knots in a thunderstorm.

events.cz_name: COASTAL WATERS FROM SOUTHWEST PASS OF THE MISSISSIPPI RIVER TO PORT FOURCHON LOUISIANA FROM 20 TO 60 NM
events.event_narrative: KMDJ AWOS recorded a wind gust of 61 mph.
Golf ball size hail reported 3 miles east of Amite. Picture relayed through broadcast media. Event time was estimated based on radar.

Two inch diameter hail was reported about 10 miles east of Amite. Several small hail reports were also received from the Independence area. The report was relayed through the Tangipahoa Parish Emergency Manager.
Baseball size hail was reported near Wilmer. Time of the event was estimated by radar. Photo was relayed by broadcast media.
Quarter size hail was reported 4 miles southeast of Kentwood. The report was relayed by broadcast media.
Golfball size hail was reported in downtown Franklinton.

A weak tornado touched down just northwest of the community of Tangipahoa. Approximately a dozen large hardwood trees, mainly oaks, were uprooted or trunks snapped. Path length approximately one quarter mile. Path width 50 yards. The tornado was ranked an EF1 on the Enhanced Fujita scale with an estimated maximum wind speed of 95 mph. Time of the event was based on radar.
A porch roof was blown off a home at Louisiana Highway 447 and Courtney Road in Walker.
A tree was reported blown down onto the eastbound side of U.S. Highway 190 on the Four Mile Bridge near Lottie.
Thunderstorm wind gusts downed a pine tree in Baywood.
Quarter size hail reported in Centreville. Event time was estimated by radar.
Quarter size hail was reported in Diamondhead. Event time was estimated from radar.

The tornado initially touched down just west of Mississippi Highway 27 southwest of Tylertown, moved moved northeast across the highway uprooting a few trees and snapping large tree limbs. The tornado moved east-northeast across East Lexie Road with the greatest damage near Ginntown Road. Heavy tree damage was noted in this area with dozens of trees uprooted or snapped. One home had a total loss of the roof and one exterior wall collapsed inward. Two individuals sustained superficial injuries and were treated on scene. A few other mobile homes had minor damage to undercarriage and roofing. A metal building had more than 80 percent of its roof removed. Minor damage also occurred to the roof of a church. The tornado crossed the intersection of Mississippi Highway 48 and Purvis Road before lifting. The tornado was rated EF1 with an estimated peak wind of 105 mph. Path length was 5 miles and maximum width 250 yards. Event time was estimated based on radar.
Two trees were blown down off of Whitaker Road less than one mile from the Mississippi-Louisiana state line.
Roof damage and damage to a shed was reported near the intersection of Fenn Road and Miller Road. Event time estimated based on radar.
Ping pong ball sized hail was reported at the South of the Border Gas Station northwest of Spillman.
An amateur radio operator relayed a report of one inch diameter hail and estimated winds of 50 mph from west of St. Francisville.
Dime to penny size hail was reported in Pine Grove by the Parish Emergency Manager.
Quarter size hail was reported in Milldale.
A few trees were reported blown down by thunderstorm winds west-northwest of Wakefield.
A few trees were reported blown down north of Spillman.
Golf ball size hail was reported in Slaughter. Event time was based on radar.
A Baton Rouge television meteorologist relayed a video of a roof blown off of a trailer near Louisiana Highway 77 and Fannie Mae Road in Grosse Tete.

A tornado touched down in Kenner near the intersection of Audubon Ct and 3rd St. It moved toward the northeast causing damage to roofs and power poles. It lifted as it neared the intersection of James St. and Pollock Plaza.

The tornado touched down in the Prairieville area just west of Airline Hwy causing roof damage and knocking down an exterior wall at Gold's Gym. It then crossed Airline Hwy causing additional roof and siding damage to several other businesses. From there the tornado continued northeastward into a residential area causing damage to roofs, sheds, and patios. It lifted as it approached Oak Grove Parkway.

The tornado touched down in a wooded area between Grantham and McLin Roads southwest of Livingston.  In this area, it snapped trees and caused roof damage consistent with an EF-1. As it moved northeastward, it strengthened and widened. The tornado completely removed the roof structure of one home on Circle Drive and another on West Railroad Street, consistent with an EF-2. The tornado is believed to have been its strongest as it approached North Willow Street. Here, it removed the entire roof structure of a home and collapsed an exterior wall of a home. Maximum wind speeds in this area were estimated to be 125 mph. The tornado then weakened as it moved into a mostly wooded area, but continued to cause damage to trees and a few roofs, lifting as it approached the intersection of North Doyle Road and Edgar Mizell Road.

A strong tornado moved out of Assumption Parish into St James Parish causing significant damage to trees as it approached the Mississippi River. After crossing the river, the tornado moved through the Sugar Hill RV Park where numerous travel trailers were tossed and destroyed. Two fatalities and approximately 75 injuries occurred at the RV park. An EF scale rating of EF-2 was assigned to the damage at and in the vicinity of the RV park. The tornado weakened as it continued northeastward, snapping trees and causing minor property damage. It dissipated as it reached Airline Highway. St. James Parish Emergency Management reported 25 to 50 homes were total losses and a public housing complex had major damage. The tornado's peak intensity of EF-3 occurred in Assumption Parish.

A weak tornado touched down near Montpelier and tracked northeast shifting a mobile home off its block piers and damaging the roof.  It also destroyed a metal shed and snapped a few small trees. It lifted near Jackson Lane. Maximum wind speed was estimated near 85 mph.

A strong tornado touched down just southwest of Paincourtville and moved northeast. Near the junction of LA Hwy 1, LA Hwy 308, and LA Hwy 70, there was considerable damage to residential and commercial buildings consistent with an EF-2 to a two story apartment building, hardware store, and commercial business. The tornado reached maximum strength as it moved along LA 1/LA 308, causing major damage to an area of small frame houses and mobile homes. In this area, the 2nd floor of a well-constructed brick home was nearly removed. This damage was consistent with wind speeds near 140 mph, or EF-3. The tornado continued moving to the northeast and crossed into St. James Parish.

A strong tornado touched down in the LaPace area, just south of Airline Hwy near a church, removing much of its roof covering. It moved northeast through a retail area causing damage consistent with an EF-1 before moving through several densely populated subdivisions. In the Carrollwood subdivision, mostly superficial roof and tree damage was observed. It strengthened as it moved into the Riverland Heights subdivision, moving roughly parallel to Greenwood Drive where many homes suffered roof damage and a few lost portions of the roof structure. It continued intensifying as it moved into the Cambridge area. Here, a few homes and duplexes suffered partial to total loss of roof structure and decking, along with partial collapse of exterior walls consistent with estimated winds around 120 mph.  The tornado was strongest in the Palmetto and Indigo Estates areas. Near the intersection of Nicole and Gail Streets, 2 single story homes suffered complete roof loss as well as total failure of most exterior walls. A third home lost about half of its second floor. Damage in this area was consistent with strong EF-2 winds near 130 mph. The tornado then weakened as it crossed Interstates 10 and 55. It continued to cause tree damage until it reached the intersection of Frenier Rd and US Hwy 51, where it lifted.

A tornadic waterspout spawned from the same parent supercell as the LaPlace tornado came on shore from Lake Pontchartrain near Lacombe. Due to inaccessibility, the first damage was noted near a plant nursery at Powell Street and Pinchon St where a greenhouse was damaged. The tornado moved northeast across Hwy 190 and into a residential area. In this area, several homes suffered superficial damage to shingles, fascia, and a few broken windows. Some minor tree damage was also observed. Maximum wind speeds were estimated near 80 mph.
In Ama, straight line winds lifted a patio cover over a house, dropping it in the front yard.

The tornado caused intermittent damage along its track near White Castle. Damage consisted of peeled back tin roofs, damage to power lines, and large tree branches downed. Maximum wind speeds were estimated near 65 mph.
Straight line wind damage in the Bayou Gauche area consisted of a garage door blown in and damage to a fence on Beau Plaza Blvd.  Vinyl siding damage was also noted on Bayou Rd.

A second weak tornado touched down in the White Castle area producing damage consisting of garage doors blown in, some light roof damage, and sheds demolished. Maximum wind speeds were estimated near 80 mph.

A tornadic waterspout spawned from the same parent supercell as the Assumption/St. James tornado moved on shore from Lake Maurepas near Akers. It snapped numerous cyprus trees before moving into Lake Pontchartrain.

A tornadic waterspout spawned from the same parent supercell as the Assumption/St. James and Akers tornadoes moved onshore from Lake Pontchartrain south of Madisonville near the end of Hwy 1077.  It destroyed a metal boat shed and caused minor fascia damage to a bar. Maximum wind speeds were estimated near 65 mph.
Pea to quarter sized hail fell for a short duration.
Quarter sized hail reported in Gulfport.
Quarter to golfball sized hail was reported in Lyman.
Golfball sized hail was reported in Wade.

A weak tornado damaged a few mobile homes and shifted one mobile home off its foundation. It also snapped trees and large branches.  It continued into Marion County before lifting. Maximum wind speeds in Pearl River County were estimated at 90 mph.

A weak tornado touched down near Donley Burks Road west of Highway 43 and moved northeastward. Minor to moderate damage was noted on 5 homes with numerous trees downed and uprooted in rural parts of the County. A tin roof was also torn off of one home. Estimated rainfall of 6 to 10 inches fell in the late evening and overnight hours in the extreme northwest portion of the county resulting in flash flooding. The runoff from the heavy rainfall caused the Pearl River to reach major flood levels in the subsequent days with the highest levels reached since spring 1983.  Flooding was also reported on the West and East Hobolochitto Creeks. Overall 46 houses and 15 mobile homes were flooded in the county by flash flooding or river flooding. Approximately 23 had minor flooding.

Heavy rainfall of 8 to 15 inches across all but far southeast Tangipahoa Parish during the overnight hours of March 10-11th resulted in numerous reports of flash flooding with many roads flooded and impassable. Flooding also developed along the Tangipahoa River and and other large streams. Over 200 roads were closed due to the flooding and bridges were washed out on Louisiana Highways 1061 and 1054. Emergency management reported approximately 1850 homes were flooded in the parish. Approximately 2800 residents had to be evacuated from areas where their residences were either flooded or isolated in flood waters. Several subdivisions in around Hammond were especially hard hit.

Major river flooding developed along the Tangipahoa River and other large streams due to the heavy rainfall. Many houses were either flooded or had access cut-off especially in the far southern sections of the parish south of Interstate 12.  Water encroached on Interstate 12 near Robert with one west bound land blocked due to high water.

Widespread heavy rainfall of 6 to 12 inches across northwest St Tammany Parish during the overnight and morning hours resulted in widespread flash flooding. Numerous roads were flooded during the night in the affected areas. High water rescues were conducted at a number of locations from flooded houses or houses isolated by flood waters. Approximately 90 people were were rescued from Camp Abbey Retreat Center on Friday - March 11. Heavy rainfall eventually caused the Baogue Falaya River, Tchefuncte River and Pearl River to reach major or historic flood levels in the few days following the heavy rainfall. A total of 625 structures within the parish were flooded from flash flooding or riverine flooding with 425 classified as major flood damage or destroyed.

Heavy rainfall across southeast Louisiana and south Mississippi caused the lower Pearl River to reach its highest level since the flooding in the spring of 1983.  The gage at Pearl River, LA reached 20.35 feet on the 14th, its 2nd highest reading on record, only surpassed by the April 1983 flood.  Several areas, including housing subdivisions, from the community of Pearl River to the southeast portion of Slidell had roadway flooding with a few houses being flooded. Water encroached onto the shoulders of Interstate 10 east of Slidell, but did not cross into the traffic lanes.

An estimated 6 to 10 inches of rain fell across southeast St Helena Parish during the late evening and overnight hours. Parish emergency management reported that 61 homes had some type of flooding and 46 roadways were damaged by flooding.
Approximately 6 to 12 inches of rain fell across all but western Livingston Parish during the overnight hours. Over 100 roads were flooded.

Rainfall of 8 to 15 inches fell across much of the parish during the evening and overnight hours. A rainfall observer near Mt. Hermon, in the far northwest section, recorded 16 inches of rainfall. The runoff from the heavy rainfall produced life threatening flash flooding in many areas of the parish. An estimated 1100 homes were flooded along with 30 churches. Approximately 80 roads were damaged or made impassable, mainly from washed out culverts and bridges.  Areas that were especially hard hit was near the Fairgrounds in Franklinton, areas of Bogalusa and areas around Mt. Hermon. Numerous search and rescue operations were conducted in the overnight hours rescue residents and motorists from flooded areas. Runoff from the rainfall eventually flowed into the large streams and rivers. Major flood levels were reached on the Bogue Chitto River at Franklinton, the highest level since the severe flooding of April 1983.  In the lower portion of the Bogue Chitto River, record crests were reach surpassing the 1983 flooding.

Runoff from the heavy rainfall caused the Bogue Chitto River to reach its highest levels since the April 1983 flood event, and surpass the 1983 flood event in the lower portion of the river. A historic crest of 21.36 feet was reached on the Bush, LA river gage on March 12.

The heavy rainfall of 6 to 14 inches across southeast Louisiana and south Mississippi caused the Pearl River to reach its highest stage since the April 1983 flood event. Low lying roadways, insufficiently raised hunting/fishing camps, and personal property were flooded. The gage at Pearl River, LA reached 20.35 feet on the 14th, its 2nd highest reading on record, only surpassed by the April 1983 flood.
A tree was blown down in the 4400 block of Bayou Black Road.

Heavy rainfall of 6 to 12 inches that fell during the overnight hours of March 10 into the morning of March 11 resulted in major and historic flooding along the Bogue Falaya and Tchefuncte Rivers of St Tammany Parish. Many areas along these rivers and tributaries experienced flooding with several hundred houses flooding. The Bogue Falaya River had a record crest at the Boston Street gage in Covington of 20.07 feet with water overtopping the Boston Street bridge. Historic flooding also occurred along the Tchefuncte River with flooding reported in several subdivisions.
Rainfall of 6 to 10 inches fell across extreme southeast Pike County resulting in flash flooding. Several roads were flooded and one roadway was reported as destroyed.
